Prioritize weight reduction, blood pressure and glycemic control, dyslipidemia management, kidney assessment, and PREVENT-based risk discussions to prevent diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and kidney disease progression. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/metabolic-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/metabolic-syndrome/article.json)
- [Hyperviscosity Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperviscosity-syndrome): Treat symptomatic hyperviscosity as an oncologic emergency: recognize retinal, mucosal bleeding, neurologic, and cardiopulmonary injury; obtain viscosity and cause-directed studies without delaying plasma exchange; then suppress the responsible paraprotein-producing or leukemic process. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperviscosity-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperviscosity-syndrome/article.json)
- [Meniere Disease](https://astramd.org/articles/meniere-disease): Diagnose Meniere disease clinically by recurrent spontaneous vertigo, documented low- to mid-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, and fluctuating unilateral aural symptoms; exclude mimics before escalating from dietary measures to intratympanic or ablative therapy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/meniere-disease/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/meniere-disease/article.json)
- [Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease](https://astramd.org/articles/hand-foot-and-mouth-disease): Hand, foot, and mouth disease is usually diagnosed clinically and managed with hydration-focused supportive care. The key physician task is to recognize dehydration, neurologic or cardiopulmonary complications, and mimics requiring lesion PCR, cerebrospinal fluid evaluation, or alternate treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hand-foot-and-mouth-disease/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hand-foot-and-mouth-disease/article.json)
- [Serotonin Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/serotonin-syndrome): Recognize serotonin syndrome clinically after a serotonergic exposure, prioritize cessation and physiologic stabilization, and rapidly identify severe hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability, or coma requiring monitored critical care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/serotonin-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/serotonin-syndrome/article.json)
- [Goodpasture Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/goodpasture-syndrome): Treat suspected Goodpasture syndrome as a pulmonary-renal emergency: stabilize hypoxemia and kidney failure, obtain anti-GBM and ANCA serologies urgently, pursue kidney biopsy when feasible, and initiate antibody removal plus immunosuppression promptly when clinical probability is high. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/goodpasture-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/goodpasture-syndrome/article.json)
- [Interstitial Lung Disease](https://astramd.org/articles/interstitial-lung-disease): Interstitial lung disease requires early separation of infection, drug toxicity, exposure-related disease, autoimmune ILD, and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis through high-resolution CT, pulmonary function testing, exposure history, serology, and multidisciplinary review to direct treatment and monitor progression. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/interstitial-lung-disease/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/interstitial-lung-disease/article.json)
- [Restrictive Lung Disease](https://astramd.org/articles/restrictive-lung-disease): Confirm true restriction with total lung capacity, then separate intrinsic parenchymal disease from obesity, neuromuscular, chest-wall, and pleural causes using diffusion capacity, imaging, oxygenation, and targeted etiologic testing. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/restrictive-lung-disease/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/restrictive-lung-disease/article.json)
- [Antiphospholipid Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/antiphospholipid-syndrome): Antiphospholipid syndrome requires a thrombotic or pregnancy morbidity phenotype plus persistent antiphospholipid antibodies. Management hinges on event type, antibody-risk profile, pregnancy status, and selection of warfarin rather than direct oral anticoagulation for arterial or triple-positive disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/antiphospholipid-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/antiphospholipid-syndrome/article.json)
- [Behçet Disease](https://astramd.org/articles/behcet-disease): Behçet disease requires phenotype-directed care: recognize clinical diagnostic patterns, urgently identify ocular, neurologic, vascular, and gastrointestinal involvement, and match immunomodulatory treatment to threatened organs rather than mucocutaneous activity alone. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/behcet-disease/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/behcet-disease/article.json)
- [Mixed Connective Tissue Disease](https://astramd.org/articles/mixed-connective-tissue-disease): Mixed connective tissue disease requires anti-U1-RNP positivity plus an evolving overlap phenotype. Initial management hinges on detecting pulmonary arterial hypertension, interstitial lung disease, inflammatory myopathy, and cardiac involvement before assigning organ-directed immunosuppression and cardiopulmonary care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/mixed-connective-tissue-disease/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/mixed-connective-tissue-disease/article.json)
- [Rib Fracture](https://astramd.org/articles/rib-fracture): Manage rib fracture as a thoracic-trauma risk problem: identify pneumothorax, hemothorax, pulmonary contusion, flail physiology, and respiratory compromise; use imaging selectively; and escalate analgesia or stabilization when pain or chest-wall instability impairs ventilation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/rib-fracture/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/rib-fracture/article.json)
- [17-Hydroxylase Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/17-hydroxylase-deficiency): Suspect 17-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency in a patient with hypertension, hypokalemia, absent or incomplete puberty, and deficient sex-steroid production; confirm the CYP17A1-related steroidogenic disorder with targeted biochemical and genetic evaluation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/17-hydroxylase-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/17-hydroxylase-deficiency/article.json)
- [21-Hydroxylase Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/21-hydroxylase-deficiency): Diagnose suspected 21-hydroxylase deficiency with properly timed 17-hydroxyprogesterone testing, urgently identify salt-wasting risk in newborns, and use cosyntropin steroid profiling and genotyping to resolve equivocal cases while guiding endocrine management and family counseling. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/21-hydroxylase-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/21-hydroxylase-deficiency/article.json)
- [Vitamin D Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/vitamin-d-deficiency): Use serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D to identify clinically meaningful deficiency, then distinguish low intake or sun exposure from malabsorption, CKD-related mineral disease, phosphate-wasting disorders, and toxicity-prone treatment settings before selecting replacement and monitoring calcium-phosphate physiology. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/vitamin-d-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/vitamin-d-deficiency/article.json)
- [Chronic Diarrhea](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-diarrhea): Use a pattern-based evaluation to identify inflammatory, malabsorptive, infectious, medication-related, postoperative, bile acid, pancreatic, and functional causes while rapidly correcting volume, electrolyte, and nutritional consequences. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-diarrhea/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-diarrhea/article.json)
- [Chronic Pain](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-pain): Chronic pain management requires phenotype-based assessment, functional goal setting, and multimodal treatment while avoiding reflexive long-term opioid escalation. Identify secondary pain generators, neuropathic features, co-occurring mental health or substance use disorders, and treatment-limiting harms before selecting pharmacologic, rehabilitative, behavioral, or procedural care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-pain/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-pain/article.json)
- [Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase-deficiency): G6PD deficiency is an X-linked red-cell enzymopathy in which oxidative infection, drugs, or fava beans can precipitate hemolysis; clinical care hinges on confirming enzyme deficiency, recognizing assay limitations, stopping exposures, treating the trigger, and preventing high-risk drug administration. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/glucose-6-phosphate-dehydrogenase-deficiency/article.json)
- [Vitamin B12 Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/vitamin-b12-deficiency): Confirm clinically meaningful cobalamin deficiency, treat neurologic or severe hematologic presentations urgently, and define whether dietary insufficiency, autoimmune gastritis, or intestinal malabsorption requires lifelong replacement and surveillance. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/vitamin-b12-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/vitamin-b12-deficiency/article.json)
- [Diffuse Axonal Injury](https://astramd.org/articles/diffuse-axonal-injury): Diffuse axonal injury should be suspected when impaired consciousness is disproportionate to CT findings after rotational head trauma. Management prioritizes severe TBI stabilization, detection of occult hemorrhagic axonal lesions with MRI, intracranial-pressure control, cautious prognostication, and early rehabilitation planning. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/diffuse-axonal-injury/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/diffuse-axonal-injury/article.json)
- [Traumatic Brain Injury](https://astramd.org/articles/traumatic-brain-injury): Traumatic brain injury management hinges on early prevention of hypoxia and hypotension, CT-defined lesion recognition, timely neurosurgical escalation, and structured surveillance for intracranial hypertension and delayed functional sequelae. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/traumatic-brain-injury/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/traumatic-brain-injury/article.json)
- [Antisocial Personality Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/antisocial-personality-disorder): Antisocial personality disorder requires longitudinal, behavior-based diagnostic assessment, separation from psychopathy and acute substance-related risk, and treatment directed at comorbid disorders, aggression, impulsivity, offending, and safety rather than an assumed medication-responsive core disorder. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/antisocial-personality-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/antisocial-personality-disorder/article.json)
- [Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder): Diagnose ADHD through DSM-5 criteria, cross-setting impairment, collateral history, and active exclusion of competing conditions. Match treatment intensity to age, impairment, comorbidity, cardiovascular risk, adverse effects, and patient preference; monitor functional response rather than symptom scores alone. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder/article.json)
- [Autism Spectrum Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/autism-spectrum-disorder): Use developmental surveillance and validated screening to trigger a comprehensive diagnostic assessment, then initiate individualized behavioral, communication, educational, and co-occurring-condition management without waiting for a single test to define care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/autism-spectrum-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/autism-spectrum-disorder/article.json)
- [Avoidant Personality Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/avoidant-personality-disorder): Diagnose avoidant personality disorder through persistent, impairing interpersonal avoidance and negative self-appraisal, while separating it from social anxiety disorder, psychotic-spectrum illness, depression, and trauma-related avoidance. Use longitudinal history, collateral data, functional assessment, and targeted treatment of comorbidity. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/avoidant-personality-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/avoidant-personality-disorder/article.json)
- [Binge-Eating Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/binge-eating-disorder): Diagnose recurrent loss-of-control eating while actively excluding compensatory behaviors and competing eating disorders, then prioritize cognitive behavioral therapy and consider lisdexamfetamine for adults with moderate to severe disease when stimulant risks are acceptable. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/binge-eating-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/binge-eating-disorder/article.json)
- [Borderline Personality Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/borderline-personality-disorder): Borderline personality disorder requires structured longitudinal diagnosis, active suicide-risk assessment, and referral to a coherent disorder-specific psychotherapy. Avoid reflexive crisis pharmacotherapy and unstructured prolonged hospitalization; target medications to independently diagnosed comorbid disorders and build a crisis plan around measurable risk and treatment continuity. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/borderline-personality-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/borderline-personality-disorder/article.json)
- [Brief Psychotic Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/brief-psychotic-disorder): Brief psychotic disorder is a time-limited diagnosis requiring abrupt psychosis, full remission within one month, and exclusion of mood, substance-related, and medical causes. Manage the presentation as first-episode psychosis while longitudinal course establishes the final diagnosis. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/brief-psychotic-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/brief-psychotic-disorder/article.json)
- [Cannabis Use Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/cannabis-use-disorder): Diagnose cannabis use disorder with a DSM-5 criterion-based assessment rather than toxicology alone, identify psychiatric and safety complications, and match treatment intensity to impairment, comorbidity, readiness, and response to evidence-based psychosocial care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cannabis-use-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cannabis-use-disorder/article.json)
- [Conduct Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/conduct-disorder): Conduct disorder requires behavior-specific assessment, careful differentiation from trauma, mood, neurodevelopmental, and substance-related conditions, and treatment that targets family, school, peer, and comorbid drivers rather than aggression alone. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/conduct-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/conduct-disorder/article.json)
- [Dependent Personality Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/dependent-personality-disorder): Dependent personality disorder requires longitudinal assessment of pervasive dependency, separation fears, and impaired autonomous decision-making while distinguishing mood, anxiety, trauma-related, cognitive, and medical drivers. Management centers on structured psychotherapy, functional goals, comorbidity treatment, and active assessment of coercion, self-harm, and suicide risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dependent-personality-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dependent-personality-disorder/article.json)
- [Illness Anxiety Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/illness-anxiety-disorder): Identify illness anxiety disorder only after a proportionate medical assessment, then replace repeated reassurance and fragmented testing with one coordinating clinician, structured cognitive-behavioral therapy, and treatment of comorbid psychiatric illness. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/illness-anxiety-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/illness-anxiety-disorder/article.json)
- [Narcissistic Personality Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/narcissistic-personality-disorder): Evaluate narcissistic personality disorder longitudinally, corroborate impairment with collateral history, assess co-occurring mood, substance, and safety syndromes, and use a structured psychotherapy-centered plan. Medication has no established role for core narcissistic pathology but may target a clearly diagnosed comorbidity. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/narcissistic-personality-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/narcissistic-personality-disorder/article.json)
- [Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/obsessive-compulsive-disorder): Manage OCD by measuring impairment and symptom severity, delivering exposure and response prevention or an SSRI, and reserving augmentation for persistent symptoms after verified adequate first-line treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/obsessive-compulsive-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/obsessive-compulsive-disorder/article.json)
- [Oppositional Defiant Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/oppositional-defiant-disorder): Evaluate persistent defiance by confirming clinically significant impairment, separating oppositional behavior from conduct disorder and chronic irritability syndromes, identifying ADHD and other comorbidity, and initiating parent-focused behavioral treatment while treating coexisting disorders with diagnosis-specific care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/oppositional-defiant-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/oppositional-defiant-disorder/article.json)
- [Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/wiskott-aldrich-syndrome): Suspect Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome in boys with persistent microthrombocytopenia, eczema, infections, autoimmunity, or lymphoid malignancy; confirm the WAS variant and expedite curative therapy planning, because hematopoietic transplantation outcomes decline with older age and severe pretransplant infection. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/wiskott-aldrich-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/wiskott-aldrich-syndrome/article.json)
- [Lynch Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/lynch-syndrome): Use universal colorectal and endometrial tumor mismatch-repair testing to identify candidates for germline evaluation, distinguish sporadic MLH1-deficient tumors, and implement gene-informed colonoscopic surveillance, cascade testing, and gynecologic risk reduction. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/lynch-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/lynch-syndrome/article.json)
- [Panic Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/panic-disorder): Evaluate acute cardiopulmonary, respiratory, toxicologic, and substance-related mimics before diagnosing panic disorder. Confirm recurrent unexpected attacks plus persistent concern or avoidance, then select disorder-focused CBT, an SSRI or SNRI, or both according to severity, preference, access, and comorbidity. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/panic-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/panic-disorder/article.json)
- [Persistent Depressive Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/persistent-depressive-disorder): Persistent depressive disorder requires confirmation of a chronic depressive course, assessment for superimposed major depression and suicide risk, and treatment planning that anticipates prolonged therapy, psychiatric comorbidity, functional impairment, and frequent incomplete response. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/persistent-depressive-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/persistent-depressive-disorder/article.json)
- [Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/premenstrual-dysphoric-disorder): Confirm PMDD with prospective daily ratings before attributing cyclic symptoms to a primary mood disorder. Distinguish PMDD from premenstrual exacerbation, assess suicidality urgently, and select SSRIs, ovulation suppression, or CBT according to symptom pattern, contraceptive needs, comorbidity, and treatment response. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/premenstrual-dysphoric-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/premenstrual-dysphoric-disorder/article.json)
- [Schizoaffective Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/schizoaffective-disorder): Schizoaffective disorder requires longitudinal confirmation of psychosis outside major mood episodes, exclusion of substance and medical causes, acute safety management, and a treatment plan that addresses persistent psychosis, the bipolar or depressive course, adherence, and suicide risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/schizoaffective-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/schizoaffective-disorder/article.json)
- [Social Anxiety Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/social-anxiety-disorder): Diagnose social anxiety disorder by persistent fear of negative evaluation, avoidance, disproportionate anxiety, and functional impairment; screen with Mini-SPIN or quantify severity with SPIN or LSAS. Select disorder-specific CBT first when acceptable, and use an SSRI when pharmacotherapy is preferred or needed. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/social-anxiety-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/social-anxiety-disorder/article.json)
- [Somatic Symptom Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/somatic-symptom-disorder): Diagnose somatic symptom disorder positively when distressing symptoms coexist with persistent, disproportionate symptom-related thoughts, anxiety, or behaviors; continue indicated medical evaluation while replacing fragmented testing with structured follow-up, functional goals, and integrated behavioral care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/somatic-symptom-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/somatic-symptom-disorder/article.json)
- [Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency): Test adults with fixed airflow obstruction, unexplained bronchiectasis, or unexplained liver disease; confirm deficiency genetically and direct management toward smoking cessation, standard organ-specific care, selective augmentation, and transplant evaluation for end-stage organ disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency/article.json)
- [Chronic Bronchitis](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-bronchitis): Chronic bronchitis should trigger confirmation of persistent airflow obstruction, assessment for competing cough syndromes and occupational exposure, and COPD-directed risk reduction. Acute worsening requires triage for hypoxemia, hypercapnia, pneumonia, and need for systemic therapy or ventilatory support. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-bronchitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/chronic-bronchitis/article.json)
- [Complement Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/complement-deficiency): Use CH50 and AH50 as the first branch point in patients with recurrent invasive infection, then confirm the implicated component and distinguish inherited deficiency from complement consumption, protein loss, impaired synthesis, or C1-inhibitor–mediated angioedema. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/complement-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/complement-deficiency/article.json)
- [Selective IgA Deficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/selective-iga-deficiency): Confirm persistent, isolated severe IgA reduction after age 4, then distinguish uncomplicated disease from impaired antibody function, evolving CVID, secondary causes, and associated infection, autoimmune, allergic, or transfusion-risk phenotypes. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/selective-iga-deficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/selective-iga-deficiency/article.json)
- [Inhalation Injury](https://astramd.org/articles/inhalation-injury): Manage inhalation injury as concurrent upper-airway edema, tracheobronchial and alveolar toxic injury, and carbon monoxide or cyanide poisoning. Early airway control, toxin-directed treatment, bronchoscopy-guided airway clearance, and serial respiratory reassessment address deterioration that can evolve after the initial examination. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/inhalation-injury/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/inhalation-injury/article.json)
- [Pressure Injury](https://astramd.org/articles/pressure-injury): Manage pressure injury by immediately removing pressure and shear, correctly distinguishing mimics, characterizing tissue loss and exudate, identifying necrosis or deep infection, and selecting debridement, moisture-balanced dressings, negative-pressure therapy, or surgical management when indicated. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pressure-injury/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pressure-injury/article.json)
- [Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis](https://astramd.org/articles/stevens-johnson-syndrome-and-toxic-epidermal-necrolysis): Suspected SJS/TEN requires immediate withdrawal of plausible culprit drugs, clinical-pathologic confirmation, severity assessment, and early multidisciplinary supportive care. Management priorities are transfer to an experienced intensive or burn-care setting, meticulous mucosal surveillance, and prevention of ocular, infectious, respiratory, and genitourinary sequelae. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/stevens-johnson-syndrome-and-toxic-epidermal-necrolysis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/stevens-johnson-syndrome-and-toxic-epidermal-necrolysis/article.json)
- [Male Urinary Retention](https://astramd.org/articles/male-urinary-retention): Rapidly decompress acute retention, identify high-risk obstructive or neurologic disease, and distinguish outlet obstruction from detrusor underactivity. Use postvoid residual trends, renal and upper-tract assessment when indicated, medication review, and a catheter-removal strategy that incorporates alpha-blockade for suspected BPH-related retention. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/male-urinary-retention/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/male-urinary-retention/article.json)
- [REM Sleep Behavior Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/rem-sleep-behavior-disorder): Confirm REM sleep behavior disorder with attended video polysomnography demonstrating REM sleep without atonia, exclude mimics and medication effects, immediately mitigate injury risk, and distinguish isolated disease from secondary RBD because isolated RBD confers substantial long-term synucleinopathy risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/rem-sleep-behavior-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/rem-sleep-behavior-disorder/article.json)
- [Cardiac Tamponade](https://astramd.org/articles/cardiac-tamponade): Cardiac tamponade is a clinical obstructive-shock syndrome requiring rapid bedside echocardiographic assessment, recognition of context-dependent sonographic findings, and urgent drainage when impaired cardiac filling causes hemodynamic compromise. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cardiac-tamponade/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cardiac-tamponade/article.json)
- [Ventricular Fibrillation](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-fibrillation): Ventricular fibrillation requires immediate defibrillation, uninterrupted high-quality CPR between shocks, protocolized epinephrine and antiarrhythmic therapy when shock-refractory, and rapid reassessment for recurrent versus persistent VF. Refractory cases require center-specific escalation decisions, including alternative pad vectors and selected extracorporeal CPR pathways. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-fibrillation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-fibrillation/article.json)
- [Posttraumatic Stress Disorder](https://astramd.org/articles/posttraumatic-stress-disorder): Diagnose PTSD with a trauma-informed clinical assessment rather than a self-report score alone, then prioritize manualized trauma-focused psychotherapy. Use symptom measures to track change, assess suicide risk directly, and avoid benzodiazepines because they do not treat core PTSD symptoms and may undermine recovery. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/posttraumatic-stress-disorder/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/posttraumatic-stress-disorder/article.json)
- [Resistant Hypertension Secondary Cause Testing](https://astramd.org/articles/resistant-hypertension-secondary-cause-testing): In apparent resistant hypertension, first confirm sustained out-of-office blood pressure elevation and treatment exposure, then pursue targeted testing for primary aldosteronism, obstructive sleep apnea, kidney disease, renovascular disease, medication effects, and selected endocrine disorders. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/resistant-hypertension-secondary-cause-testing/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/resistant-hypertension-secondary-cause-testing/article.json)
- [Hypertensive Emergency Targets](https://astramd.org/articles/hypertensive-emergency-targets): Manage hypertensive emergency by identifying the injured organ before selecting a blood pressure target. Most patients require controlled intravenous reduction of mean arterial pressure, while aortic dissection, stroke, pulmonary edema, acute coronary syndromes, and pregnancy require syndrome-specific targets and agents. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hypertensive-emergency-targets/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hypertensive-emergency-targets/article.json)
- [ACS Antithrombotic Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/acs-antithrombotic-selection): Select antithrombotic therapy in acute coronary syndrome by matching invasive timing, ischemic risk, bleeding risk, age, and chronic anticoagulation needs to an initial DAPT and anticoagulation strategy, then deliberately plan post-PCI aspirin withdrawal, P2Y12 choice, and treatment duration. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acs-antithrombotic-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acs-antithrombotic-selection/article.json)
- [Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After PCI](https://astramd.org/articles/dual-antiplatelet-therapy-after-pci): Select DAPT duration after PCI by first separating ACS from chronic coronary syndrome, then weighing bleeding risk, oral anticoagulation, and residual ischemic or procedural risk. Short DAPT followed by P2Y12 monotherapy is appropriate in selected patients; 12 months remains the ACS default. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dual-antiplatelet-therapy-after-pci/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dual-antiplatelet-therapy-after-pci/article.json)
- [Anticoagulation After Gastrointestinal Bleeding](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulation-after-gastrointestinal-bleeding): After gastrointestinal bleeding, restart anticoagulation once hemostasis is secured in most patients, because interruption lowers rebleeding exposure but increases thromboembolism and death. Timing depends on lesion control, bleeding trajectory, anticoagulant pharmacology, and the indication-specific thrombotic risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulation-after-gastrointestinal-bleeding/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulation-after-gastrointestinal-bleeding/article.json)
- [Perioperative DOAC Interruption](https://astramd.org/articles/perioperative-doac-interruption): Plan direct oral anticoagulant interruption by procedural bleeding consequence, agent, renal function, and whether neuraxial access is planned; avoid heparin bridging, confirm procedural hemostasis before restarting, and shorten time off anticoagulation whenever safely possible. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/perioperative-doac-interruption/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/perioperative-doac-interruption/article.json)
- [Atrial Fibrillation Rhythm Control Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-rhythm-control-selection): Select rhythm control by first confirming that symptom relief, AF-mediated heart failure, or early disease modification justifies sinus-rhythm pursuit; then match antiarrhythmic drugs or catheter ablation to AF pattern, heart failure status, drug tolerance, procedural risk, and anticoagulation requirements. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-rhythm-control-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-rhythm-control-selection/article.json)
- [Temporary Pacing for Bradycardia](https://astramd.org/articles/temporary-pacing-for-bradycardia): Use temporary pacing for hemodynamically unstable bradycardia, high-grade conduction disease, or impending bradyasystolic collapse when pharmacologic reversal is ineffective, inappropriate, or too slow. Select transcutaneous pacing for immediate bridging and transvenous pacing when reliable support must continue. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/temporary-pacing-for-bradycardia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/temporary-pacing-for-bradycardia/article.json)
- [Wide Complex Tachycardia](https://astramd.org/articles/wide-complex-tachycardia): Manage any adult wide complex tachycardia by first identifying instability and delivering synchronized cardioversion when needed. In stable patients, obtain a 12-lead ECG, presume ventricular tachycardia until evidence supports another mechanism, and avoid AV-nodal blockade when pre-excitation is possible. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/wide-complex-tachycardia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/wide-complex-tachycardia/article.json)
- [Aortic Stenosis Intervention Thresholds](https://astramd.org/articles/aortic-stenosis-intervention-thresholds): Replace the valve promptly for symptomatic severe aortic stenosis or LVEF below 50%; in apparently asymptomatic disease, confirm severity and use exercise testing, velocity progression, BNP, and life expectancy to determine whether surveillance remains appropriate. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/aortic-stenosis-intervention-thresholds/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/aortic-stenosis-intervention-thresholds/article.json)
- [Acute Kidney Injury Medication Adjustment](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-kidney-injury-medication-adjustment): In acute kidney injury, promptly reconcile medications, stop or reassess reversible nephrotoxins, adjust renally cleared drugs to changing kidney function, preserve essential therapy when benefits outweigh risk, and monitor creatinine, urine output, volume status, and drug concentrations when exposure is unpredictable. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-kidney-injury-medication-adjustment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-kidney-injury-medication-adjustment/article.json)
- [Prerenal Azotemia Versus Acute Tubular Injury](https://astramd.org/articles/prerenal-azotemia-versus-acute-tubular-injury): Differentiate reversible renal hypoperfusion from tubular injury by integrating exposure history, volume assessment, urine microscopy, urine indices, obstruction testing, and trajectory after hemodynamic correction. Treat life-threatening electrolyte, acid-base, uremic, and volume complications before waiting for diagnostic certainty. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/prerenal-azotemia-versus-acute-tubular-injury/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/prerenal-azotemia-versus-acute-tubular-injury/article.json)
- [Acute Interstitial Nephritis](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-interstitial-nephritis): Approach suspected acute interstitial nephritis as unexplained acute kidney injury: stop plausible culprit drugs, exclude obstructive, ischemic, infectious, and glomerular processes, and use kidney biopsy when the diagnosis or immunosuppression decision remains consequential. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-interstitial-nephritis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-interstitial-nephritis/article.json)
- [CKD Albuminuria Treatment](https://astramd.org/articles/ckd-albuminuria-treatment): Confirm persistent albuminuria with quantitative UACR, stage risk jointly with eGFR, maximize single-agent renin-angiotensin blockade, and layer SGLT2 inhibition and finerenone selectively in type 2 diabetes while monitoring potassium and kidney function. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ckd-albuminuria-treatment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ckd-albuminuria-treatment/article.json)
- [Metabolic Acidosis Anion Gap Interpretation](https://astramd.org/articles/metabolic-acidosis-anion-gap-interpretation): Interpret metabolic acidosis by confirming the primary process, calculating the serum anion gap consistently, and using gap pattern, targeted metabolites, urine indices, and exposure history to rapidly separate ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, renal failure, toxic ingestion, and bicarbonate loss. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/metabolic-acidosis-anion-gap-interpretation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/metabolic-acidosis-anion-gap-interpretation/article.json)
- [Non-Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis](https://astramd.org/articles/non-anion-gap-metabolic-acidosis): A practical workup for hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis: confirm the acid-base disorder, identify gastrointestinal versus renal bicarbonate loss, use potassium and urinary ammonium surrogates appropriately, and recognize renal tubular acidosis, kidney dysfunction, urinary diversion, and chloride-rich fluid exposure. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/non-anion-gap-metabolic-acidosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/non-anion-gap-metabolic-acidosis/article.json)
- [Hypernatremia Free Water Replacement](https://astramd.org/articles/hypernatremia-free-water-replacement): A volume-status and duration-based approach to calculate free water deficit, select enteral or intravenous replacement, protect perfusion first, account for ongoing losses, and titrate serum sodium monitoring to avoid both undercorrection and unsafe overcorrection. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hypernatremia-free-water-replacement/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hypernatremia-free-water-replacement/article.json)
- [Hypokalemia Replacement and Monitoring](https://astramd.org/articles/hypokalemia-replacement-and-monitoring): Triage hypokalemia by severity, symptoms, ECG findings, and ability to take oral therapy; replace potassium safely, correct magnesium and ongoing losses, and use urine potassium with acid-base status to identify renal wasting or extrarenal loss. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hypokalemia-replacement-and-monitoring/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hypokalemia-replacement-and-monitoring/article.json)
- [Hypomagnesemia Replacement](https://astramd.org/articles/hypomagnesemia-replacement): Choose intravenous magnesium for severe or symptomatic deficiency, correct concurrent potassium and calcium resistance, then distinguish gastrointestinal from renal losses to prevent recurrence. Replacement must be adjusted for kidney function, ongoing losses, infusion toxicity, and culprit medications. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hypomagnesemia-replacement/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hypomagnesemia-replacement/article.json)
- [Acute Hypercalcemia Management](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-hypercalcemia-management): Manage acute hypercalcemia by confirming biologically relevant calcium elevation, assessing severity and volume status, restoring euvolemia, initiating rapid calcium-lowering therapy when indicated, and directing definitive treatment by the PTH-dependent or PTH-independent mechanism. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-hypercalcemia-management/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-hypercalcemia-management/article.json)
- [Noninvasive Ventilation Failure Criteria](https://astramd.org/articles/noninvasive-ventilation-failure-criteria): Recognize NIV failure through serial physiology rather than oxygen saturation alone. Escalate promptly for worsening gas exchange, rising work of breathing, impaired consciousness, hemodynamic instability, or persistently high HACOR risk—especially in hypoxemic respiratory failure and moderate-to-severe ARDS. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/noninvasive-ventilation-failure-criteria/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/noninvasive-ventilation-failure-criteria/article.json)
- [High-Flow Nasal Oxygen Escalation](https://astramd.org/articles/high-flow-nasal-oxygen-escalation): Escalate beyond high-flow nasal oxygen when oxygenation, respiratory effort, mental status, or hemodynamics worsen despite treatment; serial ROX assessment can identify patients needing prompt intubation evaluation before prolonged noninvasive support masks clinical deterioration. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/high-flow-nasal-oxygen-escalation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/high-flow-nasal-oxygen-escalation/article.json)
- [Asthma Exacerbation Discharge Criteria](https://astramd.org/articles/asthma-exacerbation-discharge-criteria): Discharge after an asthma exacerbation requires sustained clinical improvement after treatment, objective airflow assessment when feasible, no ongoing respiratory distress, relapse-risk assessment, controller prescribing, inhaler technique review, and prompt outpatient follow-up rather than reliance on transient symptom relief alone. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/asthma-exacerbation-discharge-criteria/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/asthma-exacerbation-discharge-criteria/article.json)
- [Severe Asthma Biologic Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/severe-asthma-biologic-selection): Select an asthma biologic only after confirming severe asthma, correcting modifiable drivers, documenting exacerbation burden, and matching allergic or type 2 biomarkers, oral corticosteroid dependence, and relevant comorbidities to a single targeted agent. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/severe-asthma-biologic-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/severe-asthma-biologic-selection/article.json)
- [Pleural Effusion Thoracentesis Indications](https://astramd.org/articles/pleural-effusion-thoracentesis-indications): Perform diagnostic thoracentesis for a safely accessible effusion without a clear systemic cause, especially when infection, malignancy, or another exudative process is possible. Use ultrasound to establish procedural feasibility, obtain paired serum studies, and let fluid pH, microbiology, and cytology determine urgent drainage or tissue diagnosis. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pleural-effusion-thoracentesis-indications/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pleural-effusion-thoracentesis-indications/article.json)
- [Pleural Fluid Interpretation](https://astramd.org/articles/pleural-fluid-interpretation): Interpret pleural fluid by first identifying infection requiring drainage, then applying Light criteria, correcting pseudoexudates, and directing targeted tests for malignancy, tuberculosis, chylothorax, and other high-consequence etiologies. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pleural-fluid-interpretation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pleural-fluid-interpretation/article.json)
- [Parapneumonic Effusion Drainage Criteria](https://astramd.org/articles/parapneumonic-effusion-drainage-criteria): Drain parapneumonic effusions when pleural fluid is purulent, microbiologically positive, markedly acidotic, or anatomically large or loculated. Use immediate blood-gas pH measurement after diagnostic thoracentesis to distinguish patients likely to resolve with antibiotics from those requiring image-guided tube drainage and escalation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/parapneumonic-effusion-drainage-criteria/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/parapneumonic-effusion-drainage-criteria/article.json)
- [Hemoptysis Airway and Imaging Strategy](https://astramd.org/articles/hemoptysis-airway-and-imaging-strategy): Manage hemoptysis by physiologic threat rather than reported volume: protect oxygenation and isolate the bleeding lung first, then use contrast-enhanced CT angiography in stable patients to identify cause, laterality, and target vessels for embolization. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hemoptysis-airway-and-imaging-strategy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hemoptysis-airway-and-imaging-strategy/article.json)
- [Pulmonary Nodule Follow-Up Thresholds](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-nodule-follow-up-thresholds): Choose the management pathway before applying a size cutoff: Fleischner thresholds apply to incidental CT nodules, whereas Lung-RADS governs screening findings. Nodule attenuation, size, multiplicity, prior stability, growth, and pretest malignancy probability determine surveillance, PET/CT, tissue sampling, or surgical diagnosis. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-nodule-follow-up-thresholds/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-nodule-follow-up-thresholds/article.json)
- [Obstructive Sleep Apnea Diagnostic Testing](https://astramd.org/articles/obstructive-sleep-apnea-diagnostic-testing): Select home sleep apnea testing only for medically uncomplicated adults with a high likelihood of moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea; use attended polysomnography when comorbidity, alternate sleep pathology, hypoventilation risk, or a nondiagnostic home study could change management. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/obstructive-sleep-apnea-diagnostic-testing/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/obstructive-sleep-apnea-diagnostic-testing/article.json)
- [Shock Hemodynamic Assessment](https://astramd.org/articles/shock-hemodynamic-assessment): Assess shock by confirming impaired perfusion, rapidly defining the dominant hemodynamic phenotype with bedside ultrasound and dynamic testing, then escalating to invasive monitoring when initial resuscitation fails or mixed cardiopulmonary physiology makes further fluid, vasopressor, or inotrope decisions uncertain. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/shock-hemodynamic-assessment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/shock-hemodynamic-assessment/article.json)
- [Vasopressor Weaning](https://astramd.org/articles/vasopressor-weaning): Wean vasopressors only after sustained perfusion and correction of the shock driver, using protocolized dose reductions with MAP monitoring. In septic shock receiving norepinephrine plus vasopressin, discontinuation order remains uncertain; avoid treating either sequence as mortality-determining. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/vasopressor-weaning/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/vasopressor-weaning/article.json)
- [Lactate Interpretation](https://astramd.org/articles/lactate-interpretation): Interpret lactate as a dynamic marker of metabolic stress, hypoperfusion, and impaired clearance—not a stand-alone measure of tissue hypoxia. Use the initial value to identify high-risk shock, then reassess perfusion, organ function, and trajectory to direct escalation without pursuing normalization blindly. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/lactate-interpretation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/lactate-interpretation/article.json)
- [Spontaneous Breathing Trial Failure](https://astramd.org/articles/spontaneous-breathing-trial-failure): Spontaneous breathing trial failure should trigger targeted reassessment of respiratory load, cardiac reserve, diaphragm function, airway protection, secretion burden, and sedation rather than repeated unstructured trials. Distinguish failure of unsupported breathing from extubation risk after a passed trial. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/spontaneous-breathing-trial-failure/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/spontaneous-breathing-trial-failure/article.json)
- [Sedation Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/sedation-selection): For mechanically ventilated adults, set a measurable light-sedation target, treat pain and reversible agitation drivers, and generally select propofol or dexmedetomidine rather than benzodiazepine infusions. Hemodynamic trajectory, need for rapid awakening, and bradycardia risk determine the preferred nonbenzodiazepine agent. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sedation-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sedation-selection/article.json)
- [Delirium Assessment in the ICU](https://astramd.org/articles/delirium-assessment-in-the-icu): Use a structured arousal-first approach: establish wakefulness with RASS, then screen assessable ICU patients serially with CAM-ICU or ICDSC. A positive screen should trigger medication, physiologic, infectious, neurologic, and environmental review rather than reflex antipsychotic treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/delirium-assessment-in-the-icu/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/delirium-assessment-in-the-icu/article.json)
- [Red Cell Transfusion Thresholds](https://astramd.org/articles/red-cell-transfusion-thresholds): Use a restrictive hemoglobin threshold for most hemodynamically stable hospitalized adults, but distinguish acute myocardial infarction, cardiac surgery, orthopedic surgery, and preexisting cardiovascular disease, where trial populations and current recommendations support different decision thresholds. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/red-cell-transfusion-thresholds/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/red-cell-transfusion-thresholds/article.json)
- [Refeeding Syndrome Prevention](https://astramd.org/articles/refeeding-syndrome-prevention): Identify patients with recent nutritional deprivation before calories are increased, obtain baseline phosphate, potassium, and magnesium, limit initial carbohydrate-energy exposure, provide thiamine, and use early electrolyte surveillance to slow feeding and correct clinically consequential shifts. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/refeeding-syndrome-prevention/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/refeeding-syndrome-prevention/article.json)
- [Nutrition Initiation in Critical Illness](https://astramd.org/articles/nutrition-initiation-in-critical-illness): Initiate enteral nutrition early once shock is controlled and gastrointestinal perfusion is credible, then advance cautiously according to nutritional risk, measured or estimated energy needs, tolerance, and the route’s safety profile. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/nutrition-initiation-in-critical-illness/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/nutrition-initiation-in-critical-illness/article.json)
- [Inpatient Insulin Regimen Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/inpatient-insulin-regimen-selection): Select insulin by acuity, nutritional reliability, prior diabetes treatment, and glucose trajectory. Use IV insulin for critical illness, scheduled subcutaneous insulin for sustained ward hyperglycemia, and correction-only therapy selectively for new, mild stress hyperglycemia while preventing hypoglycemia during changing intake. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/inpatient-insulin-regimen-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/inpatient-insulin-regimen-selection/article.json)
- [Steroid-Induced Hyperglycemia](https://astramd.org/articles/steroid-induced-hyperglycemia): Adjust insulin to the glucocorticoid’s timing and glucose pattern, prioritize postprandial surveillance, treat persistent hyperglycemia with scheduled insulin, and reduce insulin promptly as steroid exposure falls to prevent hypoglycemia. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/steroid-induced-hyperglycemia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/steroid-induced-hyperglycemia/article.json)
- [SGLT2 Inhibitor Associated Ketoacidosis](https://astramd.org/articles/sglt2-inhibitor-associated-ketoacidosis): Suspect ketoacidosis—not merely gastrointestinal illness or postoperative stress—in any SGLT2 inhibitor user with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dyspnea, or malaise, regardless of glucose. Confirm with beta-hydroxybutyrate and acid-base testing, stop the drug, and treat as diabetic ketoacidosis with early carbohydrate replacement. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sglt2-inhibitor-associated-ketoacidosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sglt2-inhibitor-associated-ketoacidosis/article.json)
- [HHS Fluid Management](https://astramd.org/articles/hhs-fluid-management): Manage HHS by restoring intravascular volume before insulin, tracking osmolality and sodium to prevent overly rapid tonicity shifts, replacing potassium as needed, and individualizing crystalloid rate for cardiac or renal vulnerability. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hhs-fluid-management/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hhs-fluid-management/article.json)
- [Diabetes Medication Selection in CKD](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetes-medication-selection-in-ckd): Select glucose-lowering therapy in type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease by prioritizing SGLT2 inhibitors for kidney and heart failure protection, adding GLP-1 receptor agonists for cardiovascular and glycemic benefit, and considering finerenone for albuminuric disease with potassium surveillance. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetes-medication-selection-in-ckd/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetes-medication-selection-in-ckd/article.json)
- [GLP-1 Therapy Adverse Effects](https://astramd.org/articles/glp-1-therapy-adverse-effects): Manage GLP-1 receptor agonist adverse effects by distinguishing expected dose-related gastrointestinal intolerance from pancreatitis, obstruction, gastroparesis, biliary disease, and perioperative aspiration risk. Escalation phase, severe persistent symptoms, and planned anesthesia require targeted medication and procedural decisions. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/glp-1-therapy-adverse-effects/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/glp-1-therapy-adverse-effects/article.json)
- [Thyrotoxicosis Diagnostic Testing](https://astramd.org/articles/thyrotoxicosis-diagnostic-testing): Confirm biochemical thyrotoxicosis with TSH and free thyroid hormones, then distinguish hormone overproduction from destructive or exogenous release using TRAb and uptake-pattern testing to direct definitive management. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/thyrotoxicosis-diagnostic-testing/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/thyrotoxicosis-diagnostic-testing/article.json)
- [Thyroid Storm Treatment Sequence](https://astramd.org/articles/thyroid-storm-treatment-sequence): Treat suspected thyroid storm as an ICU emergency: resuscitate and treat the trigger while rapidly blocking adrenergic effects, hormone synthesis, hormone release, peripheral conversion, and enterohepatic recirculation in a timed sequence. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/thyroid-storm-treatment-sequence/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/thyroid-storm-treatment-sequence/article.json)
- [Adrenal Crisis](https://astramd.org/articles/adrenal-crisis): Treat suspected adrenal crisis immediately with parenteral hydrocortisone and isotonic saline; obtain diagnostic blood samples first only if this does not delay therapy. Continue stress-dose glucocorticoid replacement, correct hypoglycemia and electrolyte abnormalities, identify the precipitant, and transition only after hemodynamic and clinical stabilization. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/adrenal-crisis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/adrenal-crisis/article.json)
- [Primary Aldosteronism Screening Interpretation](https://astramd.org/articles/primary-aldosteronism-screening-interpretation): Interpret primary aldosteronism screening by assessing aldosterone and renin together, accounting for potassium status and medications, then selecting confirmatory testing or direct subtype evaluation when the biochemical phenotype is unequivocal. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/primary-aldosteronism-screening-interpretation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/primary-aldosteronism-screening-interpretation/article.json)
- [Acute Pancreatitis](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-pancreatitis): Use lactated Ringer’s–based, goal-directed rather than aggressive early resuscitation, reassess severity and volume status frequently, and restore oral or enteral nutrition early to avoid unnecessary fasting and parenteral nutrition. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-pancreatitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-pancreatitis/article.json)
- [ERCP in Acute Pancreatitis](https://astramd.org/articles/ercp-in-acute-pancreatitis): ERCP is a therapeutic, not routine diagnostic, procedure in acute pancreatitis. Perform urgent biliary drainage for cholangitis, use selective intervention for persistent obstruction, and avoid routine early ERCP when neither is present because it adds procedural risk without demonstrated benefit. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ercp-in-acute-pancreatitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ercp-in-acute-pancreatitis/article.json)
- [Acute Cholangitis Biliary Drainage](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-cholangitis-biliary-drainage): Biliary drainage timing is determined by physiologic severity and response to initial resuscitation. Perform urgent decompression for organ dysfunction, early drainage for moderate disease, and reserve antibiotics-alone management for improving mild cholangitis without persistent obstruction. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-cholangitis-biliary-drainage/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-cholangitis-biliary-drainage/article.json)
- [Variceal Bleeding Initial Management](https://astramd.org/articles/variceal-bleeding-initial-management): Treat suspected acute variceal bleeding as a portal-hypertensive emergency: resuscitate without overtransfusion, immediately start vasoactive therapy and antibiotic prophylaxis, then perform therapeutic endoscopy after hemodynamic stabilization, generally within 12 hours. Identify patients needing early or salvage portal decompression. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/variceal-bleeding-initial-management/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/variceal-bleeding-initial-management/article.json)
- [Hepatic Encephalopathy Treatment Escalation](https://astramd.org/articles/hepatic-encephalopathy-treatment-escalation): Escalate hepatic encephalopathy care by protecting the airway in severe impairment, correcting reversible precipitants, using lactulose as first-line therapy, and adding rifaximin for recurrent overt episodes. Persistent or recurrent encephalopathy requires reassessment for ongoing triggers, treatment adherence, and portosystemic shunting. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hepatic-encephalopathy-treatment-escalation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hepatic-encephalopathy-treatment-escalation/article.json)
- [Hepatorenal Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/hepatorenal-syndrome): Diagnose HRS-AKI early in decompensated cirrhosis by confirming AKI, correcting reversible precipitants, and excluding structural kidney disease. Use albumin-directed volume assessment and timely vasoconstrictor therapy while urgently pursuing liver-transplant evaluation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hepatorenal-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hepatorenal-syndrome/article.json)
- [Acute Liver Failure Transfer Criteria](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-liver-failure-transfer-criteria): Transfer patients with acute liver failure immediately to a liver transplant center when INR is at least 1.5 with encephalopathy, or when severe acute liver injury is rapidly progressing toward these features. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-liver-failure-transfer-criteria/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-liver-failure-transfer-criteria/article.json)
- [Mechanical Ventilation Liberation](https://astramd.org/articles/mechanical-ventilation-liberation): Liberate invasive ventilation through a daily, coordinated readiness assessment: reverse the indication for intubation, minimize sedation, perform a spontaneous breathing trial, then separately judge airway protection, secretion clearance, and need for prophylactic post-extubation support. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/mechanical-ventilation-liberation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/mechanical-ventilation-liberation/article.json)
- [Abnormal Liver Test Patterns](https://astramd.org/articles/abnormal-liver-test-patterns): Interpret abnormal liver tests by separating hepatocellular, cholestatic, and mixed injury, assessing bilirubin and INR for urgency, then directing serology, imaging, medication review, and selective biopsy toward the most likely competing etiologies. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/abnormal-liver-test-patterns/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/abnormal-liver-test-patterns/article.json)
- [Iron Deficiency Anemia Gastrointestinal Evaluation](https://astramd.org/articles/iron-deficiency-anemia-gastrointestinal-evaluation): Confirm iron deficiency before attributing anemia to gastrointestinal blood loss, then use patient sex, menopausal status, symptoms, and initial endoscopic findings to select bidirectional endoscopy, celiac testing, noninvasive infection testing, or small-bowel evaluation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/iron-deficiency-anemia-gastrointestinal-evaluation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/iron-deficiency-anemia-gastrointestinal-evaluation/article.json)
- [IBD Flare Infection Testing](https://astramd.org/articles/ibd-flare-infection-testing): Test symptomatic inflammatory bowel disease flares for enteric infection before attributing symptoms to inflammatory activity. Stool pathogen testing and C. difficile assays direct therapy, while fecal calprotectin, inflammatory markers, endoscopy, and imaging distinguish active mucosal disease from complications or functional symptoms. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ibd-flare-infection-testing/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ibd-flare-infection-testing/article.json)
- [Community-Acquired Pneumonia Admission Criteria](https://astramd.org/articles/community-acquired-pneumonia-admission-criteria): Determine CAP disposition by separating outpatient suitability from physiologic instability, then use PSI for mortality-oriented site-of-care assessment and ATS/IDSA severe-CAP criteria to identify patients needing ICU-level monitoring, ventilatory support, or vasopressors. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/community-acquired-pneumonia-admission-criteria/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/community-acquired-pneumonia-admission-criteria/article.json)
- [Aspiration Pneumonitis Versus Aspiration Pneumonia](https://astramd.org/articles/aspiration-pneumonitis-versus-aspiration-pneumonia): Differentiate chemical lung injury after macroaspiration from bacterial aspiration pneumonia by exposure, tempo, trajectory, and complications; then prioritize airway protection, observation, standard pneumonia therapy when infection is likely, and prevention of recurrent aspiration. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/aspiration-pneumonitis-versus-aspiration-pneumonia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/aspiration-pneumonitis-versus-aspiration-pneumonia/article.json)
- [Antibiotic De-escalation in Sepsis](https://astramd.org/articles/antibiotic-de-escalation-in-sepsis): For patients started on empiric broad-spectrum therapy for suspected sepsis, reassess infection likelihood, microbiology, source control, and clinical trajectory at 48–72 hours to stop unnecessary treatment, narrow active therapy, and use serial procalcitonin selectively to shorten exposure. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/antibiotic-de-escalation-in-sepsis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/antibiotic-de-escalation-in-sepsis/article.json)
- [MRSA Nasal Screening for Pneumonia](https://astramd.org/articles/mrsa-nasal-screening-for-pneumonia): Use MRSA nasal PCR or swab testing to narrow empiric anti-MRSA therapy in pneumonia when pretest risk is meaningful, while obtaining respiratory cultures in severe disease. A negative screen supports early withdrawal of MRSA coverage; a positive screen does not establish MRSA pneumonia. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/mrsa-nasal-screening-for-pneumonia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/mrsa-nasal-screening-for-pneumonia/article.json)
- [Complicated UTI Antibiotic Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/complicated-uti-antibiotic-selection): Select empiric therapy after obtaining urine culture, triage for systemic illness and obstruction, then narrow to susceptibility-directed treatment. For clinically improving adults receiving effective therapy, 5–7 days of a fluoroquinolone or 7 days of a nonfluoroquinolone is generally preferred over 10–14 days. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/complicated-uti-antibiotic-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/complicated-uti-antibiotic-selection/article.json)
- [Pyelonephritis Imaging Indications](https://astramd.org/articles/pyelonephritis-imaging-indications): Do not image a first, uncomplicated presentation of acute pyelonephritis. Obtain urgent imaging when obstruction, severe illness, high-risk host factors, or failure to improve raises concern for a drainable or gas-forming complication. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pyelonephritis-imaging-indications/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pyelonephritis-imaging-indications/article.json)
- [Cellulitis Antibiotic Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/cellulitis-antibiotic-selection): Select therapy by first separating nonpurulent cellulitis from abscess-associated infection, then matching route and spectrum to systemic illness, MRSA risk, immune status, source control needs, and clinical response after 48 hours. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cellulitis-antibiotic-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cellulitis-antibiotic-selection/article.json)
- [Native Joint Septic Arthritis](https://astramd.org/articles/native-joint-septic-arthritis): Manage suspected native joint septic arthritis as a drainage-and-antibiotic emergency: obtain blood and synovial cultures immediately, start empiric intravenous therapy after sampling unless sepsis mandates earlier treatment, and arrange urgent source control based on joint, purulence, clinical trajectory, and structural damage. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/native-joint-septic-arthritis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/native-joint-septic-arthritis/article.json)
- [Meningitis Empiric Antibiotic Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/meningitis-empiric-antibiotic-selection): Choose empiric therapy by acquisition setting, age, immune status, and neurosurgical hardware exposure; obtain blood cultures and CSF promptly, but do not delay antibiotics for imaging or lumbar puncture when either will defer treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/meningitis-empiric-antibiotic-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/meningitis-empiric-antibiotic-selection/article.json)
- [Transient Ischemic Attack Evaluation](https://astramd.org/articles/transient-ischemic-attack-evaluation): Treat suspected transient ischemic attack as a time-sensitive cerebrovascular emergency: establish whether infarction or a high-risk mechanism is present, complete brain, vascular, and cardiac evaluation promptly, initiate mechanism-appropriate prevention, and reserve discharge for patients with a completed expedited pathway. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/transient-ischemic-attack-evaluation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/transient-ischemic-attack-evaluation/article.json)
- [ICH Blood Pressure Management](https://astramd.org/articles/ich-blood-pressure-management): In acute spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage, rapidly achieve smooth systolic blood pressure control near 140 mm Hg while avoiding overshoot hypotension, marked variability, and delays during the early hematoma-expansion window. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ich-blood-pressure-management/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ich-blood-pressure-management/article.json)
- [Anticoagulant Reversal in Intracerebral Hemorrhage](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulant-reversal-in-intracerebral-hemorrhage): Treat anticoagulant-associated intracerebral hemorrhage as a time-critical hematoma-expansion emergency: identify the agent and last dose, send agent-relevant assays without delaying treatment, administer targeted reversal promptly, and coordinate blood-pressure management, repeat imaging, and neurosurgical assessment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulant-reversal-in-intracerebral-hemorrhage/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulant-reversal-in-intracerebral-hemorrhage/article.json)
- [Acute Headache Imaging](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-headache-imaging): Urgent neuroimaging is indicated when acute headache has thunderclap onset, focal deficits, altered consciousness, fever, papilledema, pregnancy or puerperium, cancer, immunosuppression, coagulopathy, trauma, or a progressive new pattern. Test selection should follow the suspected vascular, infectious, pressure-related, or sellar emergency. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-headache-imaging/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-headache-imaging/article.json)
- [Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Diagnostic Testing](https://astramd.org/articles/subarachnoid-hemorrhage-diagnostic-testing): Evaluate suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage with immediate noncontrast CT, using headache timing and CT interpretation quality to determine whether lumbar puncture, CT angiography, or vascular imaging is still required. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/subarachnoid-hemorrhage-diagnostic-testing/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/subarachnoid-hemorrhage-diagnostic-testing/article.json)
- [First Seizure Workup](https://astramd.org/articles/first-seizure-workup): Evaluate a first adult seizure by first excluding ongoing neurologic, toxic-metabolic, infectious, cardiac, and structural emergencies; then use eyewitness semiology, ECG, targeted laboratory testing, early EEG, and epilepsy-protocol MRI to classify recurrence risk and determine whether antiseizure treatment is justified. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/first-seizure-workup/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/first-seizure-workup/article.json)
- [Guillain-Barré Respiratory Monitoring](https://astramd.org/articles/guillain-barre-respiratory-monitoring): Guillain-Barré syndrome can progress rapidly to ventilatory failure despite modest limb weakness. Use serial bedside respiratory mechanics, bulbar assessment, and autonomic monitoring to identify patients needing ICU transfer and elective intubation before secretion failure, hypercapnia, or emergency airway loss. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/guillain-barre-respiratory-monitoring/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/guillain-barre-respiratory-monitoring/article.json)
- [Myasthenic Crisis Treatment Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/myasthenic-crisis-treatment-selection): Select plasma exchange or IVIG immediately for crisis or imminent respiratory and bulbar failure, while securing the airway, treating precipitants, and sequencing corticosteroids to avoid early worsening. Choice depends on physiologic urgency, access, contraindications, prior response, and complications. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/myasthenic-crisis-treatment-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/myasthenic-crisis-treatment-selection/article.json)
- [Spinal Cord Compression](https://astramd.org/articles/spinal-cord-compression): Urgent spinal imaging and parallel management preserve neurologic function when cord or cauda equina compression is suspected. This guide distinguishes malignant, traumatic, infectious, degenerative, and neuraxial causes; selects MRI versus CT myelography; and directs immediate decompression, corticosteroid, radiation, and surgical escalation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/spinal-cord-compression/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/spinal-cord-compression/article.json)
- [Acute Vertigo Evaluation](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-vertigo-evaluation): Evaluate acute vertigo by syndrome and examination target, not symptom quality. In continuous vestibular symptoms with spontaneous nystagmus, trained HINTS-plus examination can identify central patterns that warrant stroke imaging and management despite an early negative MRI. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-vertigo-evaluation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-vertigo-evaluation/article.json)
- [VTE Anticoagulation Duration](https://astramd.org/articles/vte-anticoagulation-duration): Select anticoagulation duration after venous thromboembolism by classifying the provoking context, estimating recurrence and bleeding risk, and reassessing persistent risks. Most transiently provoked events require 3 months; unprovoked, recurrent, and active cancer-associated VTE commonly warrant extended therapy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/vte-anticoagulation-duration/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/vte-anticoagulation-duration/article.json)
- [Cancer-Associated Thrombosis](https://astramd.org/articles/cancer-associated-thrombosis): Select anticoagulation for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism by balancing recurrence risk, bleeding-prone tumor location, renal function, platelet count, drug interactions, oral absorption, and the feasibility of sustained treatment for at least 6 months. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cancer-associated-thrombosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cancer-associated-thrombosis/article.json)
- [Thrombocytopenia Initial Workup](https://astramd.org/articles/thrombocytopenia-initial-workup): Confirm that thrombocytopenia is real, identify bleeding or thrombosis requiring immediate action, then use the smear, clinical setting, medication exposure, and accompanying cytopenias to separate peripheral destruction from impaired production and urgent consumptive syndromes. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/thrombocytopenia-initial-workup/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/thrombocytopenia-initial-workup/article.json)
- [DIC Laboratory Interpretation](https://astramd.org/articles/dic-laboratory-interpretation): Interpret suspected disseminated intravascular coagulation by integrating a triggering disorder with serial platelet count, PT, fibrinogen, and fibrin-related markers; use a validated score to identify overt disease while actively excluding mimics that require fundamentally different treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dic-laboratory-interpretation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dic-laboratory-interpretation/article.json)
- [Neutropenic Fever Antibiotics](https://astramd.org/articles/neutropenic-fever-antibiotics): Select empiric therapy immediately after cultures by separating unstable or prolonged profound neutropenia from clinically stable low-risk presentations, then individualize coverage for resistant Gram-negative colonization, suspected focus, and indications for anti-MRSA or antifungal escalation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/neutropenic-fever-antibiotics/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/neutropenic-fever-antibiotics/article.json)
- [Tumor Lysis Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/tumor-lysis-syndrome): Risk-stratify before cytoreductive therapy by malignancy biology, disease burden, baseline uric acid, renal function, and treatment potency; use hydration, urate lowering, and intensive biochemical surveillance to prevent arrhythmia, acute kidney injury, and dialysis-requiring metabolic collapse. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/tumor-lysis-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/tumor-lysis-syndrome/article.json)
- [Sickle Cell Acute Chest Syndrome](https://astramd.org/articles/sickle-cell-acute-chest-syndrome): Treat suspected acute chest syndrome as a potentially progressive pulmonary emergency: admit, establish oxygenation and respiratory trajectory, obtain chest imaging and transfusion readiness, begin analgesia, cautious hydration, lung expansion therapy, and antibiotics, then escalate promptly for refractory hypoxemia or multilobar deterioration. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sickle-cell-acute-chest-syndrome/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sickle-cell-acute-chest-syndrome/article.json)
- [Gout Flare Treatment in CKD](https://astramd.org/articles/gout-flare-treatment-in-ckd): Treat acute gout promptly while excluding septic arthritis and avoiding renal and cardiorenal toxicity. In chronic kidney disease, select colchicine cautiously, favor targeted or systemic glucocorticoids when appropriate, reserve IL-1 blockade for refractory contraindicated cases, and continue long-term urate control. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/gout-flare-treatment-in-ckd/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/gout-flare-treatment-in-ckd/article.json)
- [Bronchiolitis Oxygen and Admission Criteria](https://astramd.org/articles/bronchiolitis-oxygen-and-admission-criteria): Use respiratory effort, feeding safety, apnea history, risk factors, and persistent hypoxemia—not an isolated pulse-oximeter value—to determine disposition. For typical U.S. practice, initiate oxygen below 90%, reassess clinically after stabilization, and discontinue continuous monitoring once oxygen needs and work of breathing improve. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/bronchiolitis-oxygen-and-admission-criteria/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/bronchiolitis-oxygen-and-admission-criteria/article.json)
- [Pediatric Croup Treatment](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-croup-treatment): Treat croup severity at the bedside: give single-dose dexamethasone for children seeking care, add nebulized epinephrine for stridor at rest or increased work of breathing, observe after epinephrine, and escalate promptly when hypoxemia, exhaustion, or poor response suggests impending airway failure.
