[Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-croup-treatment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-croup-treatment/article.json)
- [Pediatric Asthma Escalation](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-asthma-escalation): Escalate pediatric asthma care according to response to initial bronchodilation, oxygenation, work of breathing, and trajectory. This guide defines practical triggers for intravenous magnesium, continuous albuterol, noninvasive support, PICU transfer, intubation planning, and avoidance of low-value rescue therapies. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-asthma-escalation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-asthma-escalation/article.json)
- [Pediatric UTI Testing](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-uti-testing): Diagnose pediatric urinary tract infection by pairing an appropriately collected urine culture with urinalysis evidence of inflammation, while using collection method, age, illness severity, and imaging triggers to avoid contamination-driven treatment and identify obstructive or recurrent disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-uti-testing/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-uti-testing/article.json)
- [Neonatal Jaundice Phototherapy Thresholds](https://astramd.org/articles/neonatal-jaundice-phototherapy-thresholds): For infants born at 35 weeks’ gestation or later, initiate phototherapy using the 2022 AAP hour-specific total serum bilirubin threshold matched to gestational age and bilirubin neurotoxicity risk factors, then use the bilirubin-to-threshold difference to determine discharge follow-up and escalation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/neonatal-jaundice-phototherapy-thresholds/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/neonatal-jaundice-phototherapy-thresholds/article.json)
- [Postpartum Hemorrhage Treatment Sequence](https://astramd.org/articles/postpartum-hemorrhage-treatment-sequence): Treat postpartum hemorrhage as simultaneous resuscitation and source control: quantify loss, assess tone, trauma, tissue, and thrombin, give early tranexamic acid, escalate rapidly from uterotonics to tamponade or operative control, and replace fibrinogen before severe coagulopathy develops. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/postpartum-hemorrhage-treatment-sequence/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/postpartum-hemorrhage-treatment-sequence/article.json)
- [Ectopic Pregnancy Treatment Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/ectopic-pregnancy-treatment-selection): Select expectant management, methotrexate, or surgery by first excluding instability and rupture, then integrating pain, ultrasound findings, hCG level, follow-up reliability, and fertility priorities. Serial hCG monitoring is mandatory after nonoperative treatment because clinical deterioration requires urgent reassessment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ectopic-pregnancy-treatment-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ectopic-pregnancy-treatment-selection/article.json)
- [Preterm Labor Antenatal Treatment](https://astramd.org/articles/preterm-labor-antenatal-treatment): Select antenatal interventions by likelihood and timing of birth, gestational age, membrane status, infection or delivery indications, and neonatal-intent plan. Use a limited tocolytic bridge for steroids or transfer, magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection rather than tocolysis, and prompt delivery when maternal or fetal risks outweigh latency. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/preterm-labor-antenatal-treatment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/preterm-labor-antenatal-treatment/article.json)
- [Alcohol Withdrawal Medication Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/alcohol-withdrawal-medication-selection): Select benzodiazepines for most alcohol withdrawal, reserve phenobarbital for protocolized severe or benzodiazepine-refractory presentations, and avoid substituting adjunctive agents for seizure- and delirium-preventive therapy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/alcohol-withdrawal-medication-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/alcohol-withdrawal-medication-selection/article.json)
- [Suicide Risk Assessment and Disposition](https://astramd.org/articles/suicide-risk-assessment-and-disposition): Use a structured assessment after a positive screen to establish acute intent, plan, access to lethal means, modifiable drivers, supports, and a disposition that matches immediate safety needs. Pair discharge decisions with collaborative safety planning, lethal-means counseling, and active follow-up. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/suicide-risk-assessment-and-disposition/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/suicide-risk-assessment-and-disposition/article.json)
- [Hyponatremia Correction Limits](https://astramd.org/articles/hyponatremia-correction-limits): For symptomatic hyponatremia, achieve an early 4-6 mEq/L sodium rise to reverse cerebral edema, then limit further correction according to chronicity and osmotic demyelination risk. Unknown duration should be managed as chronic, with frequent sodium measurements and prompt relowering after excess correction. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hyponatremia-correction-limits/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hyponatremia-correction-limits/article.json)
- [Hyponatremia Overcorrection Management](https://astramd.org/articles/hyponatremia-overcorrection-management): Prevent osmotic demyelination by identifying patients at greatest risk, tracking sodium trajectory and urine output during active correction, arresting water diuresis with desmopressin, and promptly relowering sodium with electrolyte-free water when correction limits are exceeded. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hyponatremia-overcorrection-management/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hyponatremia-overcorrection-management/article.json)
- [Urine Studies in Hyponatremia](https://astramd.org/articles/urine-studies-in-hyponatremia): Use urine osmolality and spot urine sodium, obtained before therapy when feasible, to separate suppressed vasopressin states from antidiuretic water retention and to distinguish renal salt loss, extrarenal loss, SIAD, and low effective arterial volume. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/urine-studies-in-hyponatremia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/urine-studies-in-hyponatremia/article.json)
- [Hyperkalemia Emergency Treatment](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperkalemia-emergency-treatment): Treat hyperkalemia as an electrical emergency when potassium exceeds 6.0 mmol/L or ECG toxicity is present: monitor, stabilize myocardium with IV calcium, shift potassium intracellularly, remove total-body potassium, and reassess for rebound or dialysis need. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperkalemia-emergency-treatment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperkalemia-emergency-treatment/article.json)
- [AKI Urine Microscopy](https://astramd.org/articles/aki-urine-microscopy): Urine microscopy is most useful in acute kidney injury when urinalysis suggests an active sediment or the clinical course is unexplained. Freshly examined sediment can redirect evaluation toward acute tubular injury, glomerulonephritis, vasculitis, crystal nephropathy, or biopsy-confirmable interstitial disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/aki-urine-microscopy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/aki-urine-microscopy/article.json)
- [Dialysis Indications in Acute Kidney Injury](https://astramd.org/articles/dialysis-indications-in-acute-kidney-injury): Initiate kidney replacement therapy urgently for refractory electrolyte, acid-base, fluid, or uremic complications—not creatinine alone. In severe ICU-associated AKI without an emergency indication, structured surveillance and standard initiation avoid unnecessary dialysis without improving survival through accelerated treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dialysis-indications-in-acute-kidney-injury/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dialysis-indications-in-acute-kidney-injury/article.json)
- [Nephritic Syndrome Workup](https://astramd.org/articles/nephritic-syndrome-workup): Evaluate suspected nephritic syndrome by confirming glomerular hematuria, quantifying kidney injury and proteinuria, identifying immediately reversible threats, then using complement and targeted serologies to direct urgent kidney biopsy and cause-specific management. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/nephritic-syndrome-workup/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/nephritic-syndrome-workup/article.json)
- [Nephrotic Syndrome Biopsy Indications](https://astramd.org/articles/nephrotic-syndrome-biopsy-indications): Kidney biopsy is usually required for unexplained adult nephrotic syndrome, but selected patients with PLA2R-positive membranous nephropathy may avoid it. In children, steroid response, age, atypical features, genetic risk, and failure to remit determine whether biopsy changes management. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/nephrotic-syndrome-biopsy-indications/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/nephrotic-syndrome-biopsy-indications/article.json)
- [Atrial Fibrillation Anticoagulant Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-anticoagulant-selection): Select stroke-prevention therapy in atrial fibrillation by confirming the indication for long-term anticoagulation, identifying patients who require warfarin, avoiding unsupported dose reduction, and considering left atrial appendage closure only when sustained anticoagulation is not feasible. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-anticoagulant-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-anticoagulant-selection/article.json)
- [Atrial Fibrillation Rate Control](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-rate-control): For atrial fibrillation with heart failure, select rate-control therapy by hemodynamic status, ventricular function, activity-related tachycardia, and drug tolerance; a resting rate below 110 beats/min is generally a practical initial target in stable permanent AF. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-rate-control/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-fibrillation-rate-control/article.json)
- [AF Cardioversion Anticoagulation](https://astramd.org/articles/af-cardioversion-anticoagulation): For elective cardioversion of atrial fibrillation lasting 48 hours or longer or of uncertain duration, establish uninterrupted therapeutic anticoagulation for 3 weeks or exclude intracardiac thrombus by imaging, then continue anticoagulation for at least 4 weeks after restoration of sinus rhythm. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/af-cardioversion-anticoagulation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/af-cardioversion-anticoagulation/article.json)
- [Syncope Admission Criteria](https://astramd.org/articles/syncope-admission-criteria): Admit syncope patients when a serious condition is identified or suspected after focused evaluation. Use ECG, hemodynamics, cardiac history, troponin, and clinical impression to distinguish patients needing inpatient treatment from those appropriate for discharge or structured observation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/syncope-admission-criteria/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/syncope-admission-criteria/article.json)
- [Chest Pain Troponin Interpretation](https://astramd.org/articles/chest-pain-troponin-interpretation): Interpret high-sensitivity troponin with the ECG, symptom timing, serial change, and assay-specific thresholds—not as an isolated binary test—to distinguish acute myocardial infarction, acute nonischemic injury, chronic myocardial injury, and patients eligible for safe ED discharge. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/chest-pain-troponin-interpretation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/chest-pain-troponin-interpretation/article.json)
- [Acute Heart Failure Diuretic Escalation](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-heart-failure-diuretic-escalation): Use an early intravenous loop-diuretic response assessment to distinguish underdosing from true resistance, double inadequate doses promptly, then add sequential nephron blockade selectively while monitoring renal function and electrolytes. Reserve ultrafiltration for failure of a stepped pharmacologic strategy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-heart-failure-diuretic-escalation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-heart-failure-diuretic-escalation/article.json)
- [Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-embolism-risk-stratification): Risk stratification in acute pulmonary embolism separates patients requiring immediate reperfusion from those appropriate for anticoagulation, monitored escalation, or outpatient care by integrating hemodynamics, clinical severity scores, right-ventricular assessment, and cardiac biomarkers. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-embolism-risk-stratification/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-embolism-risk-stratification/article.json)
- [Pulmonary Embolism Thrombolysis Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-embolism-thrombolysis-selection): Select reperfusion therapy by hemodynamic status, RV injury, and bleeding risk: systemic thrombolysis remains standard for high-risk PE, whereas anticoagulation with monitored rescue escalation is preferred for most normotensive intermediate-risk patients. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-embolism-thrombolysis-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pulmonary-embolism-thrombolysis-selection/article.json)
- [Sepsis Vasopressor Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/sepsis-vasopressor-selection): Use norepinephrine early to restore a mean arterial pressure of at least 65 mm Hg after initial fluid resuscitation; add fixed-dose vasopressin during escalating requirements, reserve epinephrine for persistent hypotension, and reassess for cardiogenic or obstructive physiology when shock does not respond. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sepsis-vasopressor-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sepsis-vasopressor-selection/article.json)
- [Sepsis Fluid Reassessment](https://astramd.org/articles/sepsis-fluid-reassessment): After initial crystalloid resuscitation for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion, reassess perfusion, fluid responsiveness, and congestion before each additional bolus. Passive leg raising with stroke-volume or cardiac-output measurement is the most broadly applicable dynamic test; persistent hypotension requires prompt vasopressor support rather than reflexive fluid loading. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sepsis-fluid-reassessment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sepsis-fluid-reassessment/article.json)
- [ARDS Ventilator Adjustment](https://astramd.org/articles/ards-ventilator-adjustment): Adjust ARDS ventilation by protecting the functional lung: use predicted-body-weight tidal volume, enforce plateau-pressure limits, titrate PEEP against recruitment and hemodynamic cost, prone early in moderate-to-severe disease, and refer promptly for VV-ECMO when protective targets cannot sustain gas exchange. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ards-ventilator-adjustment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ards-ventilator-adjustment/article.json)
- [COPD Exacerbation Noninvasive Ventilation](https://astramd.org/articles/copd-exacerbation-noninvasive-ventilation): Use bilevel noninvasive ventilation promptly for persistent acute hypercapnic acidosis during COPD exacerbation after initial therapy, while tightly titrating oxygen and reassessing pH, PaCO2, respiratory rate, tolerance, and need for intubation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/copd-exacerbation-noninvasive-ventilation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/copd-exacerbation-noninvasive-ventilation/article.json)
- [Community-Acquired Pneumonia Antibiotics](https://astramd.org/articles/community-acquired-pneumonia-antibiotics): Select empiric community-acquired pneumonia therapy by site of care, severity, comorbidity, and validated MRSA or Pseudomonas risk—not by obsolete healthcare-associated pneumonia categories. Obtain targeted microbiology before broad therapy when results can support de-escalation or define treatment duration. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/community-acquired-pneumonia-antibiotics/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/community-acquired-pneumonia-antibiotics/article.json)
- [Diabetic Ketoacidosis Insulin and Potassium Management](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetic-ketoacidosis-insulin-and-potassium-management): In DKA, insulin reverses ketogenesis but can precipitate fatal hypokalemia. Use beta-hydroxybutyrate and acid-base criteria to guide therapy, withhold insulin when potassium is below 3.5 mEq/L, continue treatment through ketoacidotic resolution, and overlap intravenous with subcutaneous insulin. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetic-ketoacidosis-insulin-and-potassium-management/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetic-ketoacidosis-insulin-and-potassium-management/article.json)
- [DKA Transition to Subcutaneous Insulin](https://astramd.org/articles/dka-transition-to-subcutaneous-insulin): Transition from intravenous to subcutaneous insulin only after ketoacidosis has resolved, oral intake is adequate, and basal insulin timing prevents an interruption in insulin activity. Use a structured overlap, meal-linked prandial dosing, and post-transition glucose surveillance to limit rebound hyperglycemia and recurrent DKA. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dka-transition-to-subcutaneous-insulin/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dka-transition-to-subcutaneous-insulin/article.json)
- [Inpatient Hypoglycemia Treatment](https://astramd.org/articles/inpatient-hypoglycemia-treatment): Treat any inpatient glucose below 70 mg/dL immediately, then identify the medication, nutrition, organ-failure, or acute-illness trigger before recurrence occurs. Route dextrose or glucagon to mental status and enteral access, recheck promptly, revise the causative regimen, and intensify surveillance for prolonged drug-related events. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/inpatient-hypoglycemia-treatment/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/inpatient-hypoglycemia-treatment/article.json)
- [Thyroid Nodule Biopsy Thresholds](https://astramd.org/articles/thyroid-nodule-biopsy-thresholds): Use ultrasound risk stratification plus nodule size—not size alone—to select thyroid nodules for ultrasound-guided FNA. ACR TI-RADS reduces biopsy recommendations relative to ATA-based approaches; discordant imaging and cytology should prompt repeat sampling, molecular risk stratification, or diagnostic surgery rather than reassurance. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/thyroid-nodule-biopsy-thresholds/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/thyroid-nodule-biopsy-thresholds/article.json)
- [Adrenal Insufficiency Diagnostic Testing](https://astramd.org/articles/adrenal-insufficiency-diagnostic-testing): Test promptly when otherwise unexplained hypotension, volume depletion, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, abdominal pain, fever, or hypoglycemia raises concern. Draw cortisol and ACTH when feasible, but treat suspected crisis immediately, then use cosyntropin testing and ACTH-directed classification to define primary versus central disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/adrenal-insufficiency-diagnostic-testing/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/adrenal-insufficiency-diagnostic-testing/article.json)
- [Cirrhotic Ascites Diuretics](https://astramd.org/articles/cirrhotic-ascites-diuretics): Use sodium restriction and spironolactone-based diuresis for uncomplicated moderate ascites, but stop or de-escalate therapy when renal, neurologic, or electrolyte toxicity emerges. Refractory ascites requires early transition to large-volume paracentesis with albumin, TIPS selection, and transplant evaluation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cirrhotic-ascites-diuretics/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cirrhotic-ascites-diuretics/article.json)
- [Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis](https://astramd.org/articles/spontaneous-bacterial-peritonitis): Diagnose SBP with prompt diagnostic paracentesis and ascitic neutrophil count, begin empiric therapy when PMNs reach 250/mm3, prevent renal deterioration with albumin when indicated, and actively exclude secondary peritonitis when the clinical or fluid profile is atypical. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/spontaneous-bacterial-peritonitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/spontaneous-bacterial-peritonitis/article.json)
- [Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding Risk Stratification](https://astramd.org/articles/upper-gastrointestinal-bleeding-risk-stratification): Use Glasgow-Blatchford scoring at presentation to identify patients suitable for outpatient care, while recognizing that hemodynamic instability, ongoing hemorrhage, comorbidity, and suspected varices override low-complexity disposition pathways and require resuscitation and timely endoscopy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/upper-gastrointestinal-bleeding-risk-stratification/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/upper-gastrointestinal-bleeding-risk-stratification/article.json)
- [Clostridioides difficile Treatment Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/clostridioides-difficile-treatment-selection): Select therapy after confirming clinically compatible toxin-mediated disease, classify nonfulminant versus fulminant illness, favor fidaxomicin when feasible, use vancomycin when access or severity dictates, and add recurrence-prevention strategies for patients with prior episodes or high-risk features. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/clostridioides-difficile-treatment-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/clostridioides-difficile-treatment-selection/article.json)
- [Endocarditis Blood Culture Strategy](https://astramd.org/articles/endocarditis-blood-culture-strategy): Obtain adequately collected peripheral blood cultures before antibiotics whenever clinical stability permits, then use pathogen, initial culture burden, clearance, and imaging to determine whether endocarditis evaluation must escalate. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/endocarditis-blood-culture-strategy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/endocarditis-blood-culture-strategy/article.json)
- [Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteremia Workup](https://astramd.org/articles/staphylococcus-aureus-bacteremia-workup): Treat every Staphylococcus aureus blood culture as a potential endovascular or metastatic infection: document clearance, identify and control the source, evaluate for endocarditis, and reserve 14-day therapy for patients meeting every uncomplicated-bacteremia criterion. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/staphylococcus-aureus-bacteremia-workup/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/staphylococcus-aureus-bacteremia-workup/article.json)
- [Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia](https://astramd.org/articles/heparin-induced-thrombocytopenia): Use the 4Ts score before ordering HIT tests. For intermediate or high probability, stop all heparin, begin nonheparin anticoagulation, obtain an IgG-specific PF4/heparin immunoassay, and use a functional platelet-activation assay to resolve positive or discordant results. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/heparin-induced-thrombocytopenia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/heparin-induced-thrombocytopenia/article.json)
- [Iron Deficiency Anemia Thresholds](https://astramd.org/articles/iron-deficiency-anemia-thresholds): Diagnose iron deficiency anemia by integrating hemoglobin with ferritin and transferrin saturation, then adjust interpretation for inflammation, CKD, and discordant indices. A ferritin threshold of 45 ng/mL improves diagnostic sensitivity in anemic patients undergoing gastrointestinal evaluation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/iron-deficiency-anemia-thresholds/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/iron-deficiency-anemia-thresholds/article.json)
- [Giant Cell Arteritis Immediate Management](https://astramd.org/articles/giant-cell-arteritis-immediate-management): Treat suspected giant cell arteritis immediately when cranial ischemia is possible: obtain inflammatory markers and urgent diagnostic testing without delaying glucocorticoids, stratify visual and cerebrovascular threat, and add steroid-sparing therapy when prolonged immunosuppression is anticipated. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/giant-cell-arteritis-immediate-management/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/giant-cell-arteritis-immediate-management/article.json)
- [Acute Ischemic Stroke Reperfusion Selection](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-ischemic-stroke-reperfusion-selection): Select reperfusion therapy by rapidly separating hemorrhage from ischemia, identifying treatable large-vessel occlusion, estimating infarct extent, and applying time- and tissue-based criteria without delaying intravenous thrombolysis or thrombectomy when indicated. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-ischemic-stroke-reperfusion-selection/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-ischemic-stroke-reperfusion-selection/article.json)
- [Status Epilepticus Treatment Sequence](https://astramd.org/articles/status-epilepticus-treatment-sequence): Treat convulsive status epilepticus as a timed emergency: stabilize immediately, give benzodiazepine therapy promptly, load one second-line antiseizure medication if seizures persist, and escalate to ICU anesthetic management with EEG guidance for refractory or nonconvulsive status epilepticus. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/status-epilepticus-treatment-sequence/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/status-epilepticus-treatment-sequence/article.json)
- [Febrile Infant Workup](https://astramd.org/articles/febrile-infant-workup): Evaluate well-appearing febrile infants by age, urinalysis, blood culture, and inflammatory markers; reserve lumbar puncture, empiric antibiotics, and hospitalization for higher-risk profiles while preserving reliable follow-up for selected older low-risk infants. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/febrile-infant-workup/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/febrile-infant-workup/article.json)
- [Pediatric Dehydration Rehydration](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-dehydration-rehydration): Select oral rehydration for most children with mild-to-moderate dehydration, use nasogastric ORS when drinking fails, and reserve isotonic intravenous fluid for shock, deterioration, altered mental status, ileus, or failed enteral therapy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-dehydration-rehydration/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pediatric-dehydration-rehydration/article.json)
- [Preeclampsia Severe Features](https://astramd.org/articles/preeclampsia-severe-features): Severe features shift preeclampsia management from outpatient surveillance to maternal stabilization, seizure prophylaxis, blood-pressure control, fetal assessment, and delivery planning. Delivery is indicated after stabilization at 34 weeks or sooner for uncontrolled maternal or fetal deterioration; selected patients before 34 weeks may undergo inpatient expectant management. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/preeclampsia-severe-features/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/preeclampsia-severe-features/article.json)
- [Agents for Vitreous Tamponade](https://astramd.org/articles/agents-for-vitreous-tamponade): Select air, expansile gas, or silicone oil after pars plana vitrectomy by matching tamponade duration, break location, proliferative vitreoretinopathy risk, postoperative positioning feasibility, and need for air travel or repeat surgery. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/agents-for-vitreous-tamponade/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/agents-for-vitreous-tamponade/article.json)
- [Acute Anemia](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-anemia): Manage acute anemia by first identifying unstable hemorrhage or oxygen-delivery failure, then separating blood loss from hemolysis and impaired production with serial hemoglobin, reticulocyte response, smear, and targeted hemostatic testing. Transfuse to physiologic need while obtaining definitive bleeding control or cause-directed therapy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-anemia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-anemia/article.json)
- [Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura](https://astramd.org/articles/thrombotic-thrombocytopenic-purpura): Suspected immune thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura requires immediate recognition of thrombotic microangiopathy, pre-treatment ADAMTS13 sampling, empiric plasma exchange when pretest probability is high, and rapid distinction from complement-mediated HUS and secondary thrombotic microangiopathies. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/thrombotic-thrombocytopenic-purpura/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/thrombotic-thrombocytopenic-purpura/article.json)
- [Necrotizing Fasciitis](https://astramd.org/articles/necrotizing-fasciitis): Necrotizing fasciitis is a surgical emergency: recognize disproportionate pain and systemic toxicity, obtain focused laboratory assessment and selective imaging, but do not permit testing to delay operative exploration, broad intravenous antimicrobials, and serial source control. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/necrotizing-fasciitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/necrotizing-fasciitis/article.json)
- [Uterine Rupture](https://astramd.org/articles/uterine-rupture): Suspected uterine rupture requires immediate laparotomy focused on fastest fetal delivery, hemorrhage control, and assessment for repair versus hysterectomy. Prevention centers on informed TOLAC selection, avoidance of third-trimester misoprostol in scarred uteri, and recognition of high-risk uterine scars and pregnancies. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/uterine-rupture/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/uterine-rupture/article.json)
- [Geriatric Cervical Spine Injury](https://astramd.org/articles/geriatric-cervical-spine-injury): In older adults after blunt trauma, age alone makes the Canadian C-Spine Rule positive and should lower the threshold for CT-based cervical evaluation. Treat neurologic deficits, unreliable examination, and CT-detected injury as distinct pathways requiring immobilization, trauma-spine consultation, and individualized operative risk assessment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/geriatric-cervical-spine-injury/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/geriatric-cervical-spine-injury/article.json)
- [Acute and Chronic Trauma Disorders](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-and-chronic-trauma-disorders): Assess trauma-related symptoms by timing, functional impairment, suicide and substance-use risk, and structured diagnostic interview. Distinguish acute stress disorder from PTSD, offer trauma-focused psychotherapy as first-line treatment, avoid routine psychological debriefing, and address sleep, pain, TBI, and substance-use comorbidity. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-and-chronic-trauma-disorders/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acute-and-chronic-trauma-disorders/article.json)
- [Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm](https://astramd.org/articles/abdominal-aortic-aneurysm): Manage abdominal aortic aneurysm by separating suspected rupture from stable disease, confirming maximal diameter with appropriate imaging, matching surveillance to size and sex, and referring for repair when symptoms, rapid expansion, or rupture-risk thresholds outweigh procedural risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/abdominal-aortic-aneurysm/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/abdominal-aortic-aneurysm/article.json)
- [Anticoagulation](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulation): Select anticoagulant therapy by indication and the clinical setting that changes net benefit: bleeding urgency, valve status, antiphospholipid syndrome, hepatic function, cancer, and treatment duration. Use drug-specific assays and antidotes only when results will change immediate management. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/anticoagulation/article.json)
- [Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy](https://astramd.org/articles/arrhythmogenic-right-ventricular-cardiomyopathy): Diagnose ARVC by integrating ventricular arrhythmia phenotype, ECG, quantitative right-ventricular imaging, and family or genetic data; then reduce exercise exposure, assess individualized ventricular-arrhythmia risk, and select ICD-based prevention for patients whose projected risk justifies device morbidity. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/arrhythmogenic-right-ventricular-cardiomyopathy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/arrhythmogenic-right-ventricular-cardiomyopathy/article.json)
- [Atherosclerosis](https://astramd.org/articles/atherosclerosis): Manage atherosclerosis as established or high-risk subclinical ASCVD: identify the affected vascular bed, intensify LDL-C reduction, use coronary calcium selectively when treatment is uncertain, and escalate beyond statins when residual LDL-C remains at least 70 mg/dL. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/atherosclerosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/atherosclerosis/article.json)
- [Atrial Flutter](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-flutter): Atrial flutter requires rapid distinction between hemodynamic instability, typical cavotricuspid-isthmus–dependent flutter amenable to ablation, and atypical post–left atrial ablation circuits. Stroke prevention follows atrial fibrillation principles, while long-term surveillance remains essential after apparently successful flutter ablation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-flutter/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-flutter/article.json)
- [Atrial Septal Defect](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-septal-defect): Evaluate ASD by anatomic subtype, right-heart volume loading, shunt magnitude, and pulmonary vascular status. Close hemodynamically consequential defects before irreversible pulmonary vascular disease, selecting transcatheter closure only for suitable secundum anatomy and surgery for primum, most sinus venosus, coronary sinus, or associated lesions. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-septal-defect/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/atrial-septal-defect/article.json)
- [Cardiac Amyloidosis](https://astramd.org/articles/cardiac-amyloidosis): Suspect cardiac amyloidosis in otherwise unexplained increased ventricular wall thickness or restrictive heart failure, then urgently exclude AL disease before using bone-tracer imaging to diagnose ATTR noninvasively. Amyloid typing determines whether immediate plasma-cell therapy or transthyretin-directed treatment is indicated. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cardiac-amyloidosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cardiac-amyloidosis/article.json)
- [Carotid Artery Stenosis](https://astramd.org/articles/carotid-artery-stenosis): Manage carotid stenosis by first establishing whether a recent ipsilateral retinal or cerebral ischemic event is attributable to the lesion, confirming NASCET-equivalent severity, initiating intensive vascular prevention, and rapidly selecting endarterectomy or stenting only when procedural benefit exceeds risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/carotid-artery-stenosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/carotid-artery-stenosis/article.json)
- [Coarctation of the Aorta](https://astramd.org/articles/coarctation-of-the-aorta): Coarctation requires lifelong assessment for residual obstruction, hypertension, aneurysm, and associated bicuspid valve disease. Measure arm-leg pressures, define anatomy with cross-sectional imaging, intervene for hemodynamically significant obstruction, and maintain congenital cardiology surveillance after repair. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/coarctation-of-the-aorta/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/coarctation-of-the-aorta/article.json)
- [Constrictive Pericarditis](https://astramd.org/articles/constrictive-pericarditis): Constrictive pericarditis requires confirmation of ventricular interdependence, separation from restrictive myocardial disease, and classification as inflammatory and potentially reversible versus chronic fibrotic disease requiring pericardiectomy. Multimodality imaging guides the sequence of anti-inflammatory treatment, diuresis, invasive hemodynamics, and surgical referral. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/constrictive-pericarditis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/constrictive-pericarditis/article.json)
- [Dilated Cardiomyopathy](https://astramd.org/articles/dilated-cardiomyopathy): Dilated cardiomyopathy requires prompt exclusion of ischemia and disproportionate loading conditions, targeted evaluation for reversible or inherited causes, and early HFrEF-directed therapy. Cardiac MRI, family history, genetic testing, and scar assessment refine etiology, recovery potential, and arrhythmic risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dilated-cardiomyopathy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dilated-cardiomyopathy/article.json)
- [Electrocardiogram](https://astramd.org/articles/electrocardiogram): Use the 12-lead electrocardiogram as a time-sensitive diagnostic test for ischemia, rhythm and conduction disorders, then escalate discordant or high-risk findings with targeted monitoring, imaging, electrophysiology, or repeat acquisition. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/electrocardiogram/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/electrocardiogram/article.json)
- [Familial Hypercholesterolemia](https://astramd.org/articles/familial-hypercholesterolemia): Identify probable or definite familial hypercholesterolemia early, confirm etiology when genetic testing will alter family detection or risk assessment, initiate intensive LDL-C lowering, and rapidly distinguish homozygous disease requiring receptor-independent therapy or apheresis from heterozygous disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/familial-hypercholesterolemia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/familial-hypercholesterolemia/article.json)
- [Hyperlipidemia](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperlipidemia): Manage hyperlipidemia by separating established ASCVD, severe LDL-C elevation, and risk-based primary prevention; use statins as the foundation, refine borderline decisions with coronary artery calcium, and add nonstatins when LDL-C reduction is inadequate or statins are not tolerated. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperlipidemia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperlipidemia/article.json)
- [Mitral Stenosis](https://astramd.org/articles/mitral-stenosis): Mitral stenosis management hinges on confirming hemodynamic severity, distinguishing rheumatic from calcific anatomy, preventing embolism in atrial fibrillation, and selecting balloon commissurotomy only when rheumatic valve morphology and regurgitation permit durable relief. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/mitral-stenosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/mitral-stenosis/article.json)
- [Mitral Valve Prolapse](https://astramd.org/articles/mitral-valve-prolapse): Mitral valve prolapse requires management driven by mitral regurgitation burden, left-heart remodeling, symptoms, atrial fibrillation, pulmonary pressure, and a distinct ventricular arrhythmia phenotype rather than leaflet displacement alone. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/mitral-valve-prolapse/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/mitral-valve-prolapse/article.json)
- [Orthostatic Hypotension](https://astramd.org/articles/orthostatic-hypotension): Confirm a reproducible orthostatic blood-pressure fall, identify acute volume, medication, cardiac, or neurogenic drivers, and treat disabling cerebral hypoperfusion while avoiding treatment-induced supine hypertension. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/orthostatic-hypotension/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/orthostatic-hypotension/article.json)
- [Patent Ductus Arteriosus](https://astramd.org/articles/patent-ductus-arteriosus): Manage PDA by separating preterm ductal patency from a clinically consequential shunt and from persistent congenital PDA in older patients. Echocardiography establishes anatomy and physiology; treatment is reserved for hemodynamic consequences, with transcatheter closure increasingly favored when definitive intervention is required. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/patent-ductus-arteriosus/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/patent-ductus-arteriosus/article.json)
- [Pericarditis](https://astramd.org/articles/pericarditis): Manage pericarditis by first excluding tamponade and high-risk secondary causes, then confirming active pericardial inflammation, treating uncomplicated inflammatory disease, and escalating recurrent, constrictive, purulent, tuberculous, or malignant phenotypes to targeted imaging, drainage, cause-directed therapy, or expert surgical care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pericarditis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pericarditis/article.json)
- [Pulseless Electrical Activity](https://astramd.org/articles/pulseless-electrical-activity): Manage pulseless electrical activity as a nonshockable arrest: deliver uninterrupted high-quality CPR, give early epinephrine, verify true pulselessness, and simultaneously identify a reversible mechanical, metabolic, toxic, thrombotic, or hypoxic cause. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pulseless-electrical-activity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pulseless-electrical-activity/article.json)
- [Restrictive Cardiomyopathy](https://astramd.org/articles/restrictive-cardiomyopathy): Restrictive cardiomyopathy requires rapid separation from constrictive pericarditis and etiologic classification because amyloidosis, sarcoidosis, iron overload, storage disorders, and endomyocardial disease have divergent confirmatory tests, disease-directed treatments, arrhythmia risks, and transplant implications. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/restrictive-cardiomyopathy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/restrictive-cardiomyopathy/article.json)
- [Sinus Bradycardia](https://astramd.org/articles/sinus-bradycardia): Manage sinus bradycardia by first identifying hemodynamic compromise, documenting symptom-rhythm correlation, removing reversible causes, and reserving permanent pacing for clinically consequential sinus-node dysfunction rather than an isolated low heart rate. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sinus-bradycardia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sinus-bradycardia/article.json)
- [Stable Angina](https://astramd.org/articles/stable-angina): Evaluate persistent exertional chest symptoms with risk-directed anatomic or functional testing, distinguish flow-limiting obstructive disease from nonobstructive mechanisms, initiate chronic coronary disease risk reduction and antianginal therapy, and reserve invasive angiography with physiologic assessment for actionable anatomy or refractory symptoms. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/stable-angina/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/stable-angina/article.json)
- [Sudden Cardiac Death](https://astramd.org/articles/sudden-cardiac-death): Sudden cardiac death prevention requires rapid identification of arrhythmic substrate, structural heart disease, inherited syndromes, and reversible ischemic triggers, followed by individualized device, disease-directed, and post-shock management rather than reliance on isolated electrocardiographic risk markers. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sudden-cardiac-death/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sudden-cardiac-death/article.json)
- [Superficial Thrombophlebitis](https://astramd.org/articles/superficial-thrombophlebitis): Manage superficial venous thrombosis by defining thrombus extent and deep-system proximity with duplex ultrasound, excluding concurrent DVT, and reserving anticoagulation for disease with meaningful risk of extension or embolization. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/superficial-thrombophlebitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/superficial-thrombophlebitis/article.json)
- [Supraventricular Tachycardia](https://astramd.org/articles/supraventricular-tachycardia): Manage suspected SVT by first identifying instability and QRS regularity, using vagal maneuvers and adenosine for stable regular narrow-complex rhythms, avoiding inappropriate AV-nodal blockade in pre-excited arrhythmias, and offering electrophysiology study with ablation for recurrent symptomatic disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/supraventricular-tachycardia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/supraventricular-tachycardia/article.json)
- [Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy](https://astramd.org/articles/takotsubo-cardiomyopathy): Treat suspected takotsubo cardiomyopathy as acute coronary syndrome until coronary occlusion is excluded, then use ventricular pattern, hemodynamics, and cardiac MRI to distinguish mimics and direct shock management, thrombosis surveillance, and follow-up imaging. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/takotsubo-cardiomyopathy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/takotsubo-cardiomyopathy/article.json)
- [Transposition of the Great Arteries](https://astramd.org/articles/transposition-of-the-great-arteries): D-transposition requires rapid confirmation of anatomy, maintenance of effective intracardiac mixing, and neonatal anatomic repair; lifelong surveillance after arterial switch focuses on coronary obstruction, neo-aortic disease, ventricular function, and pulmonary arterial lesions. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/transposition-of-the-great-arteries/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/transposition-of-the-great-arteries/article.json)
- [Tricuspid Regurgitation](https://astramd.org/articles/tricuspid-regurgitation): Manage tricuspid regurgitation by confirming severity with an integrated echocardiographic assessment, defining primary, atrial-functional, ventricular-functional, or lead-related mechanisms, treating congestion and upstream disease, and referring symptomatic severe disease before advanced right ventricular, renal, or hepatic dysfunction limits procedural benefit. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/tricuspid-regurgitation/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/tricuspid-regurgitation/article.json)
- [Unstable Angina](https://astramd.org/articles/unstable-angina): Evaluate suspected unstable angina as a troponin-negative ischemic syndrome: obtain prompt ECG and serial high-sensitivity troponin testing, exclude infarction, then use ischemic features and risk stratification to select invasive angiography or noninvasive coronary evaluation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/unstable-angina/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/unstable-angina/article.json)
- [Varicose Veins](https://astramd.org/articles/varicose-veins): Evaluate symptomatic or advanced varicose veins with standing duplex ultrasound to define superficial reflux, obstruction, and deep venous involvement. For intervention-eligible patients with truncal reflux, endovenous ablation generally provides durable anatomic control with less recovery burden than surgery; reserve compression alone for selected circumstances. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/varicose-veins/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/varicose-veins/article.json)
- [Venous Insufficiency](https://astramd.org/articles/venous-insufficiency): Evaluate chronic venous disease with duplex ultrasound for reflux and obstruction, exclude arterial disease before compression, and match treatment to superficial reflux, deep obstruction, edema, skin injury, or active ulceration. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/venous-insufficiency/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/venous-insufficiency/article.json)
- [Ventricular Septal Defect](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-septal-defect): Use echocardiography to define ventricular septal defect anatomy and hemodynamic effect, then distinguish patients suitable for observation from those needing congenital heart disease team assessment for surgical or transcatheter closure. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-septal-defect/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-septal-defect/article.json)
- [Ventricular Tachycardia](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-tachycardia): Treat sustained wide-complex tachycardia as ventricular tachycardia until a safer alternative is established. Immediate cardioversion is required for instability; stable cases require 12-lead ECG discrimination, antiarrhythmic selection based on ventricular function and substrate, and definitive sudden-death prevention planning. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-tachycardia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ventricular-tachycardia/article.json)
- [Acanthosis Nigricans](https://astramd.org/articles/acanthosis-nigricans): Acanthosis nigricans should prompt etiologic triage rather than cosmetic treatment alone: most cases reflect obesity-associated insulin resistance, but abrupt generalized, mucosal, or nonobese presentations require evaluation for medication, endocrine, autoimmune, and malignant drivers. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acanthosis-nigricans/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acanthosis-nigricans/article.json)
- [Acne Vulgaris](https://astramd.org/articles/acne-vulgaris): Treat acne by lesion phenotype, anatomic extent, scarring risk, and treatment response. Combine mechanistically distinct topical agents, avoid antibiotic monotherapy, use brief systemic antibiotic courses when needed, and move promptly to isotretinoin for severe, scar-forming, psychosocially burdensome, or treatment-refractory disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acne-vulgaris/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acne-vulgaris/article.json)
- [Actinic Keratosis](https://astramd.org/articles/actinic-keratosis): Manage actinic keratosis by identifying lesions that require biopsy to exclude squamous cell carcinoma, then selecting lesion- or field-directed treatment based on burden, location, recurrence, tolerability, and cosmetic priorities. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/actinic-keratosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/actinic-keratosis/article.json)
- [Alopecia Areata](https://astramd.org/articles/alopecia-areata): Confirm nonscarring alopecia areata clinically and with trichoscopy, exclude infectious or inflammatory mimics when indicated, quantify scalp loss with SALT, and match localized disease to intralesional corticosteroids versus FDA-approved oral JAK inhibition for severe disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/alopecia-areata/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/alopecia-areata/article.json)
- [Androgenetic Alopecia](https://astramd.org/articles/androgenetic-alopecia): Diagnose androgenetic alopecia by patterned miniaturization, use trichoscopy to distinguish competing alopecias, and initiate durable pharmacotherapy before irreversible density loss. Treatment selection differs substantially by sex, reproductive potential, distribution, and coexisting shedding or scarring disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/androgenetic-alopecia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/androgenetic-alopecia/article.json)
- [Atopic Dermatitis](https://astramd.org/articles/atopic-dermatitis): A severity- and site-directed approach to atopic dermatitis prioritizes topical anti-inflammatory treatment, proactive relapse prevention, and timely systemic escalation when disease remains uncontrolled, sleep-disrupting, or extensive despite optimized topical care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/atopic-dermatitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/atopic-dermatitis/article.json)
- [Bullous Pemphigoid](https://astramd.org/articles/bullous-pemphigoid): Confirm bullous pemphigoid with perilesional direct immunofluorescence plus serology, assess extent and mucosal disease, and select treatment by disease control needs against corticosteroid toxicity in an often frail older population. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/bullous-pemphigoid/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/bullous-pemphigoid/article.json)
- [Contact Dermatitis](https://astramd.org/articles/contact-dermatitis): Evaluate dermatitis through a structured exposure history, distinguish irritant from allergic mechanisms, use patch testing when contact allergy is plausible, and make relevance—not test positivity alone—the basis for avoidance and occupational interventions. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/contact-dermatitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/contact-dermatitis/article.json)
- [Dermatitis Herpetiformis](https://astramd.org/articles/dermatitis-herpetiformis): Confirm suspected dermatitis herpetiformis with direct immunofluorescence of uninvolved perilesional skin, then treat the underlying gluten-sensitive enteropathy with a lifelong gluten-free diet while using dapsone for rapid control when pruritus or lesions remain active. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dermatitis-herpetiformis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dermatitis-herpetiformis/article.json)
- [Dermatomyositis](https://astramd.org/articles/dermatomyositis): Dermatomyositis requires prompt phenotyping for muscle disease, dysphagia, interstitial lung disease, and cancer risk. Combine characteristic cutaneous findings with enzyme testing, myositis serology, MRI-directed biopsy when needed, baseline pulmonary evaluation, and risk-stratified malignancy screening. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dermatomyositis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dermatomyositis/article.json)
- [Erythema Multiforme](https://astramd.org/articles/erythema-multiforme): Manage suspected erythema multiforme by first excluding Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis, then identifying herpes simplex virus, respiratory infection, or medication exposure to guide testing, lesion-directed care, referral, and prevention of recurrent disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/erythema-multiforme/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/erythema-multiforme/article.json)
- [Erythema Nodosum](https://astramd.org/articles/erythema-nodosum): Erythema nodosum requires confirmation of a septal panniculitis pattern and a targeted search for infection, sarcoidosis, inflammatory bowel disease, medication exposure, pregnancy, and systemic inflammatory disease. Management prioritizes identifying the trigger while treating pain and monitoring for atypical or persistent disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/erythema-nodosum/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/erythema-nodosum/article.json)
- [Folliculitis](https://astramd.org/articles/folliculitis): Folliculitis is best managed by separating uncomplicated bacterial disease from exposure-related, yeast-associated, eosinophilic, and scarring scalp disorders; culture, KOH examination, and biopsy are reserved for patterns in which the result changes treatment or prevents irreversible alopecia. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/folliculitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/folliculitis/article.json)
- [Hidradenitis Suppurativa](https://astramd.org/articles/hidradenitis-suppurativa): Manage hidradenitis suppurativa by separating active inflammatory lesions from irreversible tunnels and scarring, documenting severity, addressing comorbid disease, and pairing systemic anti-inflammatory therapy with lesion-directed surgery when destructive disease persists. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hidradenitis-suppurativa/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hidradenitis-suppurativa/article.json)
- [Impetigo](https://astramd.org/articles/impetigo): Manage typical impetigo clinically with lesion-directed therapy, reserving culture for atypical, recurrent, or outbreak-associated disease. Use topical treatment for limited disease, oral therapy for numerous lesions or transmission control, and identify ecthyma because it requires systemic treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/impetigo/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/impetigo/article.json)
- [Kaposi Sarcoma](https://astramd.org/articles/kaposi-sarcoma): Confirm suspected Kaposi sarcoma with lesional histology and HHV-8 LANA-1 immunohistochemistry, then define HIV status, immunosuppression, and visceral burden to select antiretroviral therapy, immunosuppression reduction, local control, or systemic therapy. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/kaposi-sarcoma/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/kaposi-sarcoma/article.json)
- [Melasma](https://astramd.org/articles/melasma): Manage melasma as a chronic, relapsing facial pigment disorder: confirm the clinical pattern, exclude inflammatory, drug-related, and dermal pigment mimics, identify hormonal and photic triggers, and use durable photoprotection with topical therapy before cautiously escalating refractory disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/melasma/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/melasma/article.json)
- [Molluscum Contagiosum](https://astramd.org/articles/molluscum-contagiosum): Molluscum contagiosum is usually a clinical diagnosis managed with observation or lesion-directed treatment, but genital disease, atypical morphology, bacterial superinfection, and extensive or refractory lesions require a different diagnostic and immunologic assessment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/molluscum-contagiosum/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/molluscum-contagiosum/article.json)
- [Onychomycosis](https://astramd.org/articles/onychomycosis): Confirm fungal infection before committing patients to prolonged therapy, obtain an adequately proximal subungual specimen, and select topical versus oral treatment by extent, organism, contraindications, interactions, and treatment goals. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/onychomycosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/onychomycosis/article.json)
- [Pemphigus Vulgaris](https://astramd.org/articles/pemphigus-vulgaris): Confirm pemphigus vulgaris with lesion-directed immunopathology, distinguish it from other blistering disorders and paraneoplastic disease, then use severity and mucosal risk to select systemic corticosteroids, rituximab-based therapy, and steroid-sparing maintenance. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pemphigus-vulgaris/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pemphigus-vulgaris/article.json)
- [Psoriasis](https://astramd.org/articles/psoriasis): Manage psoriasis by confirming the clinical phenotype, quantifying extent and life impact, identifying psoriatic arthritis and cardiometabolic comorbidity, then selecting site-directed topical therapy, phototherapy, systemic therapy, or biologic treatment according to severity, trajectory, and treatment risk. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/psoriasis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/psoriasis/article.json)
- [Pyoderma Gangrenosum](https://astramd.org/articles/pyoderma-gangrenosum): Pyoderma gangrenosum requires rapid recognition of an inflammatory ulcer pattern while actively excluding infection, vascular disease, vasculitis, and malignancy. Biopsy and cultures should precede immunosuppression when feasible; avoid traumatic debridement once pathergy is suspected. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/pyoderma-gangrenosum/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/pyoderma-gangrenosum/article.json)
- [Rosacea](https://astramd.org/articles/rosacea): Manage rosacea by phenotype rather than a fixed subtype: confirm compatible centrofacial disease, exclude mimics when morphology is atypical, treat inflammatory lesions and persistent erythema separately, and identify ocular or phymatous disease early because corneal injury and tissue remodeling require targeted escalation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/rosacea/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/rosacea/article.json)
- [Scabies](https://astramd.org/articles/scabies): Manage suspected scabies by confirming when uncertainty changes management, treating the patient and close contacts concurrently, distinguishing crusted disease early, and reassessing persistent itch for reinfestation, application failure, dermatitis, or an alternative diagnosis. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/scabies/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/scabies/article.json)
- [Seborrheic Dermatitis](https://astramd.org/articles/seborrheic-dermatitis): Manage seborrheic dermatitis clinically when distribution is typical, but perform targeted fungal testing or biopsy for atypical, refractory, or systemic presentations. Use site-directed antifungal therapy for control, brief anti-inflammatory treatment for flares, and maintenance therapy to reduce relapse. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/seborrheic-dermatitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/seborrheic-dermatitis/article.json)
- [Seborrheic Keratosis](https://astramd.org/articles/seborrheic-keratosis): Seborrheic keratosis is managed conservatively only after a sufficiently confident clinical and dermoscopic assessment. Biopsy lesions with diagnostic uncertainty or atypical features before destructive treatment, because melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and other epidermal tumors can mimic seborrheic keratosis. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/seborrheic-keratosis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/seborrheic-keratosis/article.json)
- [Sunburn](https://astramd.org/articles/sunburn): Manage sunburn by identifying blistering or systemic illness that warrants urgent assessment, avoiding further ultraviolet exposure, and using layered photoprotection to prevent recurrent injury. Broad-spectrum sunscreen, protective clothing, and sun avoidance reduce ultraviolet-associated skin damage. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sunburn/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sunburn/article.json)
- [Telogen Effluvium](https://astramd.org/articles/telogen-effluvium): Evaluate diffuse shedding by anchoring onset to a trigger, excluding patterned and inflammatory alopecia, and correcting identifiable systemic, nutritional, or medication causes. Acute telogen effluvium usually resolves after trigger removal; shedding beyond 6 months warrants reassessment for chronic disease or a competing diagnosis. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/telogen-effluvium/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/telogen-effluvium/article.json)
- [Tinea Capitis](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-capitis): Confirm suspected scalp dermatophyte infection with hair and scale microscopy or culture when feasible, begin systemic therapy because topical agents do not reach the follicular infection, identify inflammatory kerion promptly to limit permanent alopecia, and interrupt household transmission with contact assessment and sporicidal shampoo. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-capitis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-capitis/article.json)
- [Tinea Corporis](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-corporis): Manage localized tinea corporis with topical antifungal therapy after bedside confirmation when morphology is uncertain; obtain mycologic testing and reassess exposure, adherence, steroid use, and resistance when disease is extensive, recurrent, or treatment-refractory. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-corporis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-corporis/article.json)
- [Tinea Cruris](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-cruris): Confirm dermatophyte infection when morphology is atypical, recurrent, extensive, or treatment-refractory; treat limited disease with topical antifungal monotherapy, identify pedal or nail reservoirs, and escalate persistent disease to culture, speciation, susceptibility testing, and systemic therapy planning. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-cruris/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-cruris/article.json)
- [Tinea Pedis](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-pedis): Confirm atypical, chronic, or treatment-refractory foot eruptions with potassium hydroxide examination, then match topical therapy duration to interdigital versus hyperkeratotic disease. Escalate persistent disease by reassessing diagnosis, nail reservoir, adherence, immunologic risk, bacterial superinfection, and need for culture-directed evaluation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-pedis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/tinea-pedis/article.json)
- [Vitiligo](https://astramd.org/articles/vitiligo): Confirm true depigmentation, define nonsegmental versus segmental distribution and activity, screen selectively for autoimmune disease, and match topical, phototherapy, systemic, or surgical treatment to extent, site, progression, and stability. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/vitiligo/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/vitiligo/article.json)
- [Amphetamine Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/amphetamine-toxicity): Amphetamine toxicity is a clinical sympathomimetic emergency requiring rapid recognition of hyperthermia, agitation, seizures, cardiovascular ischemia or dysrhythmia, rhabdomyolysis, and co-ingestion, followed by targeted monitoring and escalation for organ-specific complications. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/amphetamine-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/amphetamine-toxicity/article.json)
- [Anticholinergic Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/anticholinergic-toxicity): Recognize the clinical antimuscarinic pattern, identify sodium-channel blockade or competing toxidromes, stabilize hyperthermia and agitation, and select physostigmine only for consequential delirium after electrocardiographic risk assessment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/anticholinergic-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/anticholinergic-toxicity/article.json)
- [Benzodiazepine Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/benzodiazepine-toxicity): Manage benzodiazepine toxicity by prioritizing airway and ventilation, actively identifying opioid, alcohol, and proconvulsant co-ingestion, and reserving flumazenil for exceptional pure exposures without seizure risk or benzodiazepine dependence. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/benzodiazepine-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/benzodiazepine-toxicity/article.json)
- [Beta-Blocker Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/beta-blocker-toxicity): Manage suspected beta-blocker toxicity as a time-critical cardiotoxic poisoning: identify conduction delay, shock, hypoglycemia, seizures, and coingestants; initiate resuscitation and monitored antidotal therapy; and escalate refractory cardiogenic shock promptly to high-dose insulin and advanced critical care. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/beta-blocker-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/beta-blocker-toxicity/article.json)
- [Calcium Channel Blocker Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/calcium-channel-blocker-toxicity): Manage suspected calcium channel blocker toxicity as a time-critical cardiovascular poisoning: establish invasive-ready monitoring, treat bradycardia and shock in parallel, begin vasopressors and high-dose insulin early for significant hypotension, and escalate refractory cardiogenic shock to mechanical circulatory support. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/calcium-channel-blocker-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/calcium-channel-blocker-toxicity/article.json)
- [Cocaine Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/cocaine-toxicity): Manage cocaine toxicity by treating agitation, hyperthermia, seizures, and cardiovascular instability immediately while evaluating chest pain and focal neurologic deficits for acute coronary syndrome, aortic dissection, and stroke. Observation is appropriate only after recurrent symptoms and acute ischemia have been excluded. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cocaine-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cocaine-toxicity/article.json)
- [Cyanide Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/cyanide-toxicity): Treat suspected severe cyanide toxicity immediately when a compatible exposure accompanies rapid neurologic or cardiovascular collapse and metabolic acidosis. Secure oxygenation and circulation, obtain targeted co-exposure testing, and give IV hydroxocobalamin without awaiting cyanide confirmation when clinical suspicion is high. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/cyanide-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/cyanide-toxicity/article.json)
- [Ethylene Glycol Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/ethylene-glycol-toxicity): Treat suspected ethylene glycol poisoning before confirmatory levels return when exposure history, high-anion-gap acidosis, osmolar gap, or oxalate crystalluria indicates evolving toxic metabolite production; use fomepizole promptly and add hemodialysis for acidosis, renal failure, or severe measured exposure. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/ethylene-glycol-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/ethylene-glycol-toxicity/article.json)
- [Lead Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/lead-toxicity): Use blood lead testing to confirm suspected exposure, identify the exposure route, remove the source promptly, and recognize severe neurologic or gastrointestinal toxicity requiring urgent specialist-directed chelation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/lead-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/lead-toxicity/article.json)
- [Methanol Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/methanol-toxicity): Suspect methanol toxicity in unexplained high-anion-gap acidosis, especially with visual symptoms or an elevated osmolar gap. Start alcohol dehydrogenase blockade and bicarbonate immediately when clinically suspected; use hemodialysis for severe acidosis, organ toxicity, or impaired clearance. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/methanol-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/methanol-toxicity/article.json)
- [Methemoglobinemia](https://astramd.org/articles/methemoglobinemia): Confirm suspected methemoglobinemia with blood-gas co-oximetry when cyanosis or low pulse oximetry is disproportionate to cardiopulmonary findings, immediately remove oxidant exposure, and use symptom-, concentration-, and oxygen-delivery risk–based antidotal treatment while avoiding methylene blue in G6PD deficiency. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/methemoglobinemia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/methemoglobinemia/article.json)
- [Organophosphate Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/organophosphate-toxicity): Treat suspected organophosphate toxicity as a clinical cholinergic emergency: protect staff, control airway and bronchorrhea, titrate atropine to a clear chest, add an oxime when indicated, and use cholinesterase testing as confirmation rather than a reason to delay resuscitation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/organophosphate-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/organophosphate-toxicity/article.json)
- [Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/selective-serotonin-reuptake-inhibitor-toxicity): SSRI overdose is usually mild but can produce serotonin toxicity, delayed seizures, QTc or QRS prolongation, dysrhythmia, and rhabdomyolysis. Triage hinges on exposure history, clonus-focused examination, serial ECG assessment, co-ingestant evaluation, supportive treatment, and prolonged monitoring when escitalopram or citalopram is involved. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/selective-serotonin-reuptake-inhibitor-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/selective-serotonin-reuptake-inhibitor-toxicity/article.json)
- [Sympathomimetic Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/sympathomimetic-toxicity): Recognize the hyperadrenergic syndrome early, stabilize agitation and hyperthermia with GABAergic sedation and cooling, then selectively investigate cardiac, neurologic, renal, and muscle complications that determine monitored versus critical-care disposition. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/sympathomimetic-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/sympathomimetic-toxicity/article.json)
- [Tricyclic Antidepressant Toxicity](https://astramd.org/articles/tricyclic-antidepressant-toxicity): Manage suspected tricyclic antidepressant toxicity by immediate airway and hemodynamic stabilization, continuous ECG monitoring, and early sodium bicarbonate for QRS widening, acidosis, dysrhythmia, or shock. Serial ECG, pH, and electrolyte results guide alkalinization and ICU-level escalation. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/tricyclic-antidepressant-toxicity/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/tricyclic-antidepressant-toxicity/article.json)
- [Acromegaly](https://astramd.org/articles/acromegaly): Diagnose acromegaly with age-adjusted IGF-1, resolve equivocal biochemistry selectively with oral glucose testing, localize the source by pituitary MRI, and tailor surgery, medical therapy, radiotherapy, and longitudinal surveillance to tumor anatomy and biochemical control. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/acromegaly/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/acromegaly/article.json)
- [Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia](https://astramd.org/articles/congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia): Evaluate suspected congenital adrenal hyperplasia by urgency and steroid pattern: immediately protect infants at risk for salt-wasting crisis, confirm 21-hydroxylase deficiency with serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone and targeted cosyntropin testing, then use mineralocorticoid replacement, glucocorticoid coverage during physiologic stress, and CYP21A2 testing selectively. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/congenital-adrenal-hyperplasia/article.json)
- [Delayed Puberty](https://astramd.org/articles/delayed-puberty): Evaluate delayed puberty by separating constitutional and functional delay from central hypogonadism and primary gonadal failure. Growth trajectory, bone age, pubertal examination, LH/FSH, and sex steroids direct targeted evaluation, timed observation, puberty induction, and long-term replacement planning. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/delayed-puberty/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/delayed-puberty/article.json)
- [Diabetic Retinopathy](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetic-retinopathy): Manage diabetic retinopathy by separating nonproliferative disease, center-involving macular edema, and proliferative complications; use OCT and targeted angiography to define threat, maintain surveillance proportional to severity, and select anti-VEGF therapy, laser, or vitrectomy when anatomy, vision, or treatment adherence changes the balance. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetic-retinopathy/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/diabetic-retinopathy/article.json)
- [Dyslipidemia](https://astramd.org/articles/dyslipidemia): Manage dyslipidemia by separating LDL-C–driven ASCVD risk from triglyceride-driven pancreatitis risk, excluding secondary causes, identifying familial disease, and escalating from maximally tolerated statins to evidence-based nonstatins according to residual risk and lipid response. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/dyslipidemia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/dyslipidemia/article.json)
- [Gastrinoma](https://astramd.org/articles/gastrinoma): Suspect gastrinoma in recurrent or refractory ulcer disease, severe reflux, or secretory diarrhea with hypergastrinemia. Confirm inappropriate gastrin secretion in an acidic stomach, protect against acid-related complications immediately, then localize and stage for multidisciplinary curative or disease-control treatment. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/gastrinoma/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/gastrinoma/article.json)
- [Glucagonoma](https://astramd.org/articles/glucagonoma): Suspect glucagonoma when necrolytic migratory erythema, weight loss, diabetes, anemia, or thrombosis coexists with marked fasting hyperglucagonemia. Confirm biochemical syndrome, stage with pancreas-protocol imaging and somatostatin receptor PET, obtain graded tissue diagnosis, and prioritize resection when feasible. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/glucagonoma/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/glucagonoma/article.json)
- [Gynecomastia](https://astramd.org/articles/gynecomastia): Evaluate gynecomastia by separating typical pubertal or drug-related disease from hypogonadism, systemic illness, hormone-secreting tumors, and male breast cancer. Focus testing on atypical, progressive, or unexplained presentations; withdraw reversible exposures and reserve surgery for persistent, consequential disease. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/gynecomastia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/gynecomastia/article.json)
- [Hashimoto Thyroiditis](https://astramd.org/articles/hashimoto-thyroiditis): Diagnose Hashimoto thyroiditis by integrating TSH/free T4 status with TPO or thyroglobulin antibodies and, when needed, ultrasound; treat thyroid hormone deficiency rather than antibody positivity, optimize levothyroxine administration before escalating dose, and intensify surveillance during pregnancy and postpartum. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hashimoto-thyroiditis/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hashimoto-thyroiditis/article.json)
- [Hirsutism](https://astramd.org/articles/hirsutism): Evaluate hirsutism by tempo, virilization, menstrual pattern, and objective androgen testing. Most cases reflect PCOS or idiopathic hyperandrogenism, but rapid progression, later onset, or marked biochemical androgen excess requires urgent exclusion of adrenal or ovarian neoplasia. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hirsutism/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hirsutism/article.json)
- [Hyperprolactinemia](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperprolactinemia): Evaluate confirmed prolactin elevation by first excluding pregnancy, medication effects, hypothyroidism, renal or hepatic failure, and assay interference; then use symptom burden, prolactin magnitude, and pituitary MRI findings to distinguish prolactinoma from stalk effect and guide definitive management. [Markdown](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperprolactinemia/article.md) · [JSON](https://astramd.org/articles/hyperprolactinemia/article.json)
